problem: Question: Consider the page reference string: 4, 0, 0, 7, 3, 6, 6, 1, 1, 0, 2, 2, 6, 1, 2, 0, 1, 5. Using LRU with a frame count of 4, what is the page fault rate (miss ratio)?
solution:
**Policy: LRU, 4 frames** (all empty at the start)

_Rule: on a fault with all frames full, evict the page used LEAST RECENTLY._

| # | Ref | Result | Evicted | Why | Frames (least recently used first) | Faults |
|---|-----|--------|---------|-----|--------|--------|
| 1 | 4 | miss | - | free frame (1/4 used) | 4 | 1 |
| 2 | 0 | miss | - | free frame (2/4 used) | 4 0 | 2 |
| 3 | 0 | hit | - | 0 already in frames | 4 0 | 2 |
| 4 | 7 | miss | - | free frame (3/4 used) | 4 0 7 | 3 |
| 5 | 3 | miss | - | free frame (4/4 used) | 4 0 7 3 | 4 |
| 6 | 6 | miss | 4 | frames full; last used 4@#1 < 0@#3 < 7@#4 < 3@#5 -> least recent = 4 | 0 7 3 6 | 5 |
| 7 | 6 | hit | - | 6 already in frames | 0 7 3 6 | 5 |
| 8 | 1 | miss | 0 | frames full; last used 0@#3 < 7@#4 < 3@#5 < 6@#7 -> least recent = 0 | 7 3 6 1 | 6 |
| 9 | 1 | hit | - | 1 already in frames | 7 3 6 1 | 6 |
| 10 | 0 | miss | 7 | frames full; last used 7@#4 < 3@#5 < 6@#7 < 1@#9 -> least recent = 7 | 3 6 1 0 | 7 |
| 11 | 2 | miss | 3 | frames full; last used 3@#5 < 6@#7 < 1@#9 < 0@#10 -> least recent = 3 | 6 1 0 2 | 8 |
| 12 | 2 | hit | - | 2 already in frames | 6 1 0 2 | 8 |
| 13 | 6 | hit | - | 6 already in frames | 1 0 2 6 | 8 |
| 14 | 1 | hit | - | 1 already in frames | 0 2 6 1 | 8 |
| 15 | 2 | hit | - | 2 already in frames | 0 6 1 2 | 8 |
| 16 | 0 | hit | - | 0 already in frames | 6 1 2 0 | 8 |
| 17 | 1 | hit | - | 1 already in frames | 6 2 0 1 | 8 |
| 18 | 5 | miss | 6 | frames full; last used 6@#13 < 2@#15 < 0@#16 < 1@#17 -> least recent = 6 | 2 0 1 5 | 9 |

**Total page faults = 9** (hits = 18 - 9 = 9, hit ratio = 9 / 18 = 0.5, fault ratio = 9 / 18 = 0.5)

**Answer: hit ratio = 0.5, fault ratio = 0.5**

problem: Head position: 89. Pending requests (cylinders): {29, 26, 39, 123, 58, 7, 209}. The previous request served was at cylinder 76. Using C-LOOK scheduling, find the total number of cylinders the head moves.
solution:
**Policy: CLOOK**

- direction: previous request 76 < head 89, so the head is moving UP
- sorted requests: [7, 26, 29, 39, 58, 123, 209]; below head 89: [7, 26, 29, 39, 58]; at/above head: [123, 209]
- C-LOOK, head moving UP, towards higher cylinders: service [123, 209], jump to the farthest pending request, continue up through [7, 26, 29, 39, 58]
- 89 -> 123: 123 - 89 = 34; running total 0 + 34 = 34
- 123 -> 209: 209 - 123 = 86; running total 34 + 86 = 120
- 209 -> 7: 209 - 7 = 202; running total 120 + 202 = 322
- 7 -> 26: 26 - 7 = 19; running total 322 + 19 = 341
- 26 -> 29: 29 - 26 = 3; running total 341 + 3 = 344
- 29 -> 39: 39 - 29 = 10; running total 344 + 10 = 354
- 39 -> 58: 58 - 39 = 19; running total 354 + 19 = 373

**Service order:** 123 -> 209 -> 7 -> 26 -> 29 -> 39 -> 58
**Total head movement = 373 cylinders**
- Average seek length = 373 / 7 = 53.29
- _Convention: this total counts the return jump of 202 cylinders. If your course excludes the jump, the total is 373 - 202 = 171._

**Answer: total head movement = 373 cylinders**

problem: Consider the following. For the reference string 6 1 6 0 5 3 4 4 7 8 2 6 with a frame count of 4, using the clock (second-chance) algorithm: find the hit ratio.
solution:
**Policy: CLOCK, 4 frames** (all empty at the start)

_Rule: on a fault with all frames full, advance the hand: a page with bit 1 gets a second chance (bit cleared), the first page with bit 0 is evicted; a hit sets the bit to 1._

| # | Ref | Result | Evicted | Why | Frames (reference bit in brackets) | Faults |
|---|-----|--------|---------|-----|--------|--------|
| 1 | 6 | miss | - | free frame (1/4 used) | 6(1) | 1 |
| 2 | 1 | miss | - | free frame (2/4 used) | 6(1) 1(1) | 2 |
| 3 | 6 | hit | - | hit, set bit of 6 to 1 | 6(1) 1(1) | 2 |
| 4 | 0 | miss | - | free frame (3/4 used) | 6(1) 1(1) 0(1) | 3 |
| 5 | 5 | miss | - | free frame (4/4 used) | 6(1) 1(1) 0(1) 5(1), hand 6 | 4 |
| 6 | 3 | miss | 6 | frames full; hand 6(1) clear, 1(1) clear, 0(1) clear, 5(1) clear, 6(0) evict | 3(1) 1(0) 0(0) 5(0), hand 1 | 5 |
| 7 | 4 | miss | 1 | frames full; hand 1(0) evict | 3(1) 4(1) 0(0) 5(0), hand 0 | 6 |
| 8 | 4 | hit | - | hit, set bit of 4 to 1 | 3(1) 4(1) 0(0) 5(0), hand 0 | 6 |
| 9 | 7 | miss | 0 | frames full; hand 0(0) evict | 3(1) 4(1) 7(1) 5(0), hand 5 | 7 |
| 10 | 8 | miss | 5 | frames full; hand 5(0) evict | 3(1) 4(1) 7(1) 8(1), hand 3 | 8 |
| 11 | 2 | miss | 3 | frames full; hand 3(1) clear, 4(1) clear, 7(1) clear, 8(1) clear, 3(0) evict | 2(1) 4(0) 7(0) 8(0), hand 4 | 9 |
| 12 | 6 | miss | 4 | frames full; hand 4(0) evict | 2(1) 6(1) 7(0) 8(0), hand 7 | 10 |

**Total page faults = 10** (hits = 12 - 10 = 2, hit ratio = 2 / 12 = 0.1667, fault ratio = 10 / 12 = 0.8333)

**Answer: hit ratio = 0.1667, fault ratio = 0.8333**

problem:
A system has 3 resource types (A, B, C) and 5 processes. The system has [4, 1, 5] instances of each type free.

| P       | Alloc A | Alloc B | Alloc C | Max A | Max B | Max C |
|---------|---------|---------|---------|-------|-------|-------|
| alpha   | 3       | 5       | 1       | 6     | 6     | 7     |
| beta    | 3       | 0       | 3       | 3     | 3     | 3     |
| gamma   | 1       | 1       | 1       | 2     | 3     | 1     |
| delta   | 1       | 1       | 0       | 7     | 8     | 0     |
| epsilon | 1       | 1       | 0       | 1     | 1     | 2     |

Using Banker's algorithm, determine whether the system is in a safe state. If it is, give a safe sequence.
solution:
**Step 1 - compute Need = Max - Allocation, row by row** (resources A, B, C)

- alpha: [6, 6, 7] - [3, 5, 1] = [3, 1, 6]
- beta: [3, 3, 3] - [3, 0, 3] = [0, 3, 0]
- gamma: [2, 3, 1] - [1, 1, 1] = [1, 2, 0]
- delta: [7, 8, 0] - [1, 1, 0] = [6, 7, 0]
- epsilon: [1, 1, 2] - [1, 1, 0] = [0, 0, 2]

**Step 2 - run the safety algorithm** (scan the processes in order; run the first one whose Need fits in Work, then add its Allocation to Work and scan again)

- Work = Available = [4, 1, 5]
- alpha: Need [3, 1, 6] vs Work [4, 1, 5]: 3<=4, 1<=1, 6>5 -> cannot run yet
- beta: Need [0, 3, 0] vs Work [4, 1, 5]: 0<=4, 3>1, 0<=5 -> cannot run yet
- gamma: Need [1, 2, 0] vs Work [4, 1, 5]: 1<=4, 2>1, 0<=5 -> cannot run yet
- delta: Need [6, 7, 0] vs Work [4, 1, 5]: 6>4, 7>1, 0<=5 -> cannot run yet
- epsilon: Need [0, 0, 2] vs Work [4, 1, 5]: 0<=4, 0<=1, 2<=5 -> all fit, run it. Work = [4, 1, 5] + Allocation [1, 1, 0] = [5, 2, 5]
- alpha: Need [3, 1, 6] vs Work [5, 2, 5]: 3<=5, 1<=2, 6>5 -> cannot run yet
- beta: Need [0, 3, 0] vs Work [5, 2, 5]: 0<=5, 3>2, 0<=5 -> cannot run yet
- gamma: Need [1, 2, 0] vs Work [5, 2, 5]: 1<=5, 2<=2, 0<=5 -> all fit, run it. Work = [5, 2, 5] + Allocation [1, 1, 1] = [6, 3, 6]
- alpha: Need [3, 1, 6] vs Work [6, 3, 6]: 3<=6, 1<=3, 6<=6 -> all fit, run it. Work = [6, 3, 6] + Allocation [3, 5, 1] = [9, 8, 7]
- beta: Need [0, 3, 0] vs Work [9, 8, 7]: 0<=9, 3<=8, 0<=7 -> all fit, run it. Work = [9, 8, 7] + Allocation [3, 0, 3] = [12, 8, 10]
- delta: Need [6, 7, 0] vs Work [12, 8, 10]: 6<=12, 7<=8, 0<=10 -> all fit, run it. Work = [12, 8, 10] + Allocation [1, 1, 0] = [13, 9, 10]

**Step 3 - conclusion**

All 5 processes can complete, so the system is in a **SAFE state**.
A safe sequence is **< epsilon, gamma, alpha, beta, delta >**.

_Safe sequences are not unique: any ordering in which each process's Need is met by the running Work vector is equally correct._

**Answer: SAFE, safe sequence < epsilon, gamma, alpha, beta, delta >**

problem:
Memory contains holes of sizes `[286, 457, 176, 521, 150]` (in KB, in this order). Processes request `[497, 483, 490, 384, 142]` KB, in that order.

Using **FIRST-fit**, show which hole serves each request and the remaining free space.
solution:
**Policy: FIRST-fit**

_Rule: scan holes in order and take the FIRST that is large enough; the leftover stays as a smaller hole. A request that fits nowhere must wait._

- holes (free KB, numbered in order): hole 1=286, hole 2=457, hole 3=176, hole 4=521, hole 5=150
- request 497: hole 1=286 < 497 no; hole 2=457 < 497 no; hole 3=176 < 497 no; hole 4=521 >= 497 fits -> first fitting hole = hole 4; 521 - 497 = 24
- request 483: hole 1=286 < 483 no; hole 2=457 < 483 no; hole 3=176 < 483 no; hole 4=24 < 483 no; hole 5=150 < 483 no -> no hole fits -> must WAIT
- request 490: hole 1=286 < 490 no; hole 2=457 < 490 no; hole 3=176 < 490 no; hole 4=24 < 490 no; hole 5=150 < 490 no -> no hole fits -> must WAIT
- request 384: hole 1=286 < 384 no; hole 2=457 >= 384 fits -> first fitting hole = hole 2; 457 - 384 = 73
- request 142: hole 1=286 >= 142 fits -> first fitting hole = hole 1; 286 - 142 = 144

**Placement:** 497 KB -> hole 4; 483 KB -> WAIT; 490 KB -> WAIT; 384 KB -> hole 2; 142 KB -> hole 1
**Remaining free space per hole:** [144, 73, 176, 24, 150]
- Sum of free space: 144 + 73 = 217, 217 + 176 = 393, 393 + 24 = 417, 417 + 150 = 567
**Total external fragmentation = 567 KB**

**Answer: 497 KB -> hole 4; 483 KB -> WAIT; 490 KB -> WAIT; 384 KB -> hole 2; 142 KB -> hole 1**

A safe sequence is **< P0, P2, P1, P3 >**.

problem:
A video transcoding farm runs on a machine with **8192-byte** pages. The page table is:

| Page | Frame |
|------|-------|
| 0    | 47    |
| 1    | 22    |
| 2    | 7     |
| 3    | 37    |
| 4    | 60    |
| 5    | 51    |

Convert logical address **9070** into its physical equivalent, showing the page number and offset.
solution:
**Step-by-step translation**

- page number = floor(9070 / 8192) = 1  (check: 1 x 8192 = 8192 <= 9070 < 16384)
- page offset = 9070 - 8192 = 878
- page table[1] = frame 22
- frame base = 22 x 8192 = 180224
- physical address = 180224 + 878 = 181102

**Physical address = 181102**

**Answer: physical address = 181102**

problem: Here is an exam question. The disk has 250 cylinders (0 to 249). Head position: 26. Queue = 62, 57, 99, 197, 9, 114. The head has just finished a request at 50. Using SCAN (elevator) scheduling, find the total head movement and the average seek length.
solution:
**Policy: SCAN**

- direction: previous request 50 > head 26, so the head is moving DOWN
- sorted requests: [9, 57, 62, 99, 114, 197]; below head 26: [9]; at/above head: [57, 62, 99, 114, 197]
- SCAN, head moving DOWN, towards cylinder 0: service [9], continue to the disk edge 0, reverse, then service [57, 62, 99, 114, 197]
- 26 -> 9: 26 - 9 = 17; running total 0 + 17 = 17
- 9 -> 0: 9 - 0 = 9; running total 17 + 9 = 26
- 0 -> 57: 57 - 0 = 57; running total 26 + 57 = 83
- 57 -> 62: 62 - 57 = 5; running total 83 + 5 = 88
- 62 -> 99: 99 - 62 = 37; running total 88 + 37 = 125
- 99 -> 114: 114 - 99 = 15; running total 125 + 15 = 140
- 114 -> 197: 197 - 114 = 83; running total 140 + 83 = 223

**Service order:** 9 -> 0 -> 57 -> 62 -> 99 -> 114 -> 197
**Total head movement = 223 cylinders**
- Average seek length = 223 / 6 = 37.17

**Answer: total head movement = 223 cylinders, average seek length = 37.17**

problem:
A system has 4 resource types (A, B, C, D) and 4 processes. Currently available: [6, 5, 3, 4].

| P  | Alloc A | Alloc B | Alloc C | Alloc D | Max A | Max B | Max C | Max D |
|----|---------|---------|---------|---------|-------|-------|-------|-------|
| P0 | 1       | 0       | 4       | 2       | 2     | 1     | 7     | 8     |
| P1 | 0       | 6       | 3       | 3       | 1     | 7     | 6     | 7     |
| P2 | 1       | 0       | 0       | 0       | 2     | 0     | 0     | 6     |
| P3 | 0       | 2       | 1       | 0       | 2     | 5     | 2     | 3     |

Determine safety using Banker's algorithm, showing the Need matrix and each Work update.
solution:
**Step 1 - compute Need = Max - Allocation, row by row** (resources A, B, C, D)

- P0: [2, 1, 7, 8] - [1, 0, 4, 2] = [1, 1, 3, 6]
- P1: [1, 7, 6, 7] - [0, 6, 3, 3] = [1, 1, 3, 4]
- P2: [2, 0, 0, 6] - [1, 0, 0, 0] = [1, 0, 0, 6]
- P3: [2, 5, 2, 3] - [0, 2, 1, 0] = [2, 3, 1, 3]

**Step 2 - run the safety algorithm** (scan the processes in order; run the first one whose Need fits in Work, then add its Allocation to Work and scan again)

- Work = Available = [6, 5, 3, 4]
- P0: Need [1, 1, 3, 6] vs Work [6, 5, 3, 4]: 1<=6, 1<=5, 3<=3, 6>4 -> cannot run yet
- P1: Need [1, 1, 3, 4] vs Work [6, 5, 3, 4]: 1<=6, 1<=5, 3<=3, 4<=4 -> all fit, run it. Work = [6, 5, 3, 4] + Allocation [0, 6, 3, 3] = [6, 11, 6, 7]
- P0: Need [1, 1, 3, 6] vs Work [6, 11, 6, 7]: 1<=6, 1<=11, 3<=6, 6<=7 -> all fit, run it. Work = [6, 11, 6, 7] + Allocation [1, 0, 4, 2] = [7, 11, 10, 9]
- P2: Need [1, 0, 0, 6] vs Work [7, 11, 10, 9]: 1<=7, 0<=11, 0<=10, 6<=9 -> all fit, run it. Work = [7, 11, 10, 9] + Allocation [1, 0, 0, 0] = [8, 11, 10, 9]
- P3: Need [2, 3, 1, 3] vs Work [8, 11, 10, 9]: 2<=8, 3<=11, 1<=10, 3<=9 -> all fit, run it. Work = [8, 11, 10, 9] + Allocation [0, 2, 1, 0] = [8, 13, 11, 9]

**Step 3 - conclusion**

All 4 processes can complete, so the system is in a **SAFE state**.
A safe sequence is **< P1, P0, P2, P3 >**.

_Safe sequences are not unique: any ordering in which each process's Need is met by the running Work vector is equally correct._

**Answer: SAFE, safe sequence < P1, P0, P2, P3 >**

problem: Q. Free blocks: 192 KB, 400 KB, 125 KB, 301 KB, 304 KB (in order). The processes need 203 KB, 186 KB, 126 KB, 421 KB, 432 KB (in order). Using first fit, show the allocation. Which processes cannot be allocated?
solution:
**Policy: FIRST-fit**

_Rule: scan holes in order and take the FIRST that is large enough; the leftover stays as a smaller hole. A request that fits nowhere must wait._

- holes (free KB, numbered in order): hole 1=192, hole 2=400, hole 3=125, hole 4=301, hole 5=304
- request 203: hole 1=192 < 203 no; hole 2=400 >= 203 fits -> first fitting hole = hole 2; 400 - 203 = 197
- request 186: hole 1=192 >= 186 fits -> first fitting hole = hole 1; 192 - 186 = 6
- request 126: hole 1=6 < 126 no; hole 2=197 >= 126 fits -> first fitting hole = hole 2; 197 - 126 = 71
- request 421: hole 1=6 < 421 no; hole 2=71 < 421 no; hole 3=125 < 421 no; hole 4=301 < 421 no; hole 5=304 < 421 no -> no hole fits -> must WAIT
- request 432: hole 1=6 < 432 no; hole 2=71 < 432 no; hole 3=125 < 432 no; hole 4=301 < 432 no; hole 5=304 < 432 no -> no hole fits -> must WAIT

**Placement:** 203 KB -> hole 2; 186 KB -> hole 1; 126 KB -> hole 2; 421 KB -> WAIT; 432 KB -> WAIT
**Remaining free space per hole:** [6, 71, 125, 301, 304]
- Sum of free space: 6 + 71 = 77, 77 + 125 = 202, 202 + 301 = 503, 503 + 304 = 807
**Total external fragmentation = 807 KB**

**Answer: cannot be allocated: 421 KB, 432 KB**

problem: Q. Processes (arrival, burst): T1 (3, 1), T2 (3, 3), T3 (5, 1), T4 (6, 3), T5 (7, 1), T6 (8, 11). Apply shortest remaining time first. Which process finishes last, and at what time?
solution:
**Algorithm: SRTF (preemptive SJF)**

**Step 1 - build the schedule**

_Rule: at every arrival and completion, run the ready process with the SHORTEST REMAINING time; preempt the running process if a shorter one is ready (ties: earlier arrival, then name)._

- t=0: no process has arrived -> CPU idle until t=3
- t=3: T1, T2 arrive; ready T1(1) < T2(3) -> run T1
- t=4: T1 completes; only T2 is ready -> run T2
- t=5: T3 arrives; ready T3(1) < T2(2) -> PREEMPT T2, run T3
- t=6: T3 completes; T4 arrives; ready T2(2) < T4(3) -> run T2
- t=7: T5 arrives; ready T2(1) = T5(1) < T4(3) (tie -> earlier arrival, then name) -> keep running T2
- t=8: T2 completes; T6 arrives; ready T5(1) < T4(3) < T6(11) -> run T5
- t=9: T5 completes; ready T4(3) < T6(11) -> run T4
- t=12: T4 completes; only T6 is ready -> run T6
- t=23: T6 completes; all processes done

**Step 2 - Gantt chart:** T1[3-4] T2[4-5] T3[5-6] T2[6-8] T5[8-9] T4[9-12] T6[12-23]

**Step 3 - per-process times** (Turnaround = Completion - Arrival; Waiting = Turnaround - Burst)

| Process | Arrival | Burst | Completion | Turnaround  | Waiting     |
|---------|---------|-------|------------|-------------|-------------|
| T1      | 3       | 1     | 4          | 4 - 3 = 1   | 1 - 1 = 0   |
| T2      | 3       | 3     | 8          | 8 - 3 = 5   | 5 - 3 = 2   |
| T3      | 5       | 1     | 6          | 6 - 5 = 1   | 1 - 1 = 0   |
| T4      | 6       | 3     | 12         | 12 - 6 = 6  | 6 - 3 = 3   |
| T5      | 7       | 1     | 9          | 9 - 7 = 2   | 2 - 1 = 1   |
| T6      | 8       | 11    | 23         | 23 - 8 = 15 | 15 - 11 = 4 |

**Step 4 - averages**

- Sum of waiting times: 0 + 2 = 2, 2 + 0 = 2, 2 + 3 = 5, 5 + 1 = 6, 6 + 4 = 10
- Average waiting time = 10 / 6 = **1.67**
- Sum of turnaround times: 1 + 5 = 6, 6 + 1 = 7, 7 + 6 = 13, 13 + 2 = 15, 15 + 15 = 30
- Average turnaround time = 30 / 6 = **5.0**

**Answer: T6 finishes last, at t = 23**

**Step 4 - averages**

- Average waiting time = 50 / 4 = **12.5**
- Sum of turnaround times: 10 + 18 = 28, 28 + 27 = 55, 55 + 28 = 83
- Average turnaround time = 83 / 4 = **20.75**

problem: I need help with this problem. Currently available: A=6, B=5, C=3, D=6. Allocation = [[1, 0, 1, 2], [3, 3, 2, 1], [0, 4, 2, 7], [2, 2, 3, 6], [1, 0, 4, 5]]. Cylinders are numbered 0-249. Head position: 157. Pending requests (cylinders): [10, 134, 151, 98, 191, 45]. The head is moving towards higher cylinder numbers. Using SCAN scheduling, find the total head movement and the average seek length.
solution:
**Policy: SCAN**

- sorted requests: [10, 45, 98, 134, 151, 191]; below head 157: [10, 45, 98, 134, 151]; at/above head: [191]
- SCAN, head moving UP, towards higher cylinders: service [191], continue to the disk edge 249, reverse, then service [151, 134, 98, 45, 10]
- 157 -> 191: 191 - 157 = 34; running total 0 + 34 = 34
- 191 -> 249: 249 - 191 = 58; running total 34 + 58 = 92
- 249 -> 151: 249 - 151 = 98; running total 92 + 98 = 190
- 151 -> 134: 151 - 134 = 17; running total 190 + 17 = 207
- 134 -> 98: 134 - 98 = 36; running total 207 + 36 = 243
- 98 -> 45: 98 - 45 = 53; running total 243 + 53 = 296
- 45 -> 10: 45 - 10 = 35; running total 296 + 35 = 331

**Service order:** 191 -> 249 -> 151 -> 134 -> 98 -> 45 -> 10
**Total head movement = 331 cylinders**
- Average seek length = 331 / 6 = 55.17

**Answer: total head movement = 331 cylinders, average seek length = 55.17**

problem:
Can you solve this step by step? A system has resource types A, B, C, D and processes P0, P1, P2, P3. The available vector is <3, 5, 2, 4>.

| Process | Alloc A | Alloc B | Alloc C | Alloc D | Max A | Max B | Max C | Max D |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| P0 | 1 | 2 | 0 | 3 | 2 | 2 | 0 | 6 |
| P1 | 2 | 0 | 0 | 2 | 3 | 0 | 1 | 6 |
| P2 | 0 | 1 | 7 | 1 | 6 | 3 | 8 | 2 |
| P3 | 0 | 2 | 2 | 0 | 0 | 5 | 8 | 0 |

P0 requests [1, 0, 0, 2]. Can the request be granted immediately?
solution:
**Step 1 - compute Need = Max - Allocation, row by row** (resources A, B, C, D)

- P0: [2, 2, 0, 6] - [1, 2, 0, 3] = [1, 0, 0, 3]
- P1: [3, 0, 1, 6] - [2, 0, 0, 2] = [1, 0, 1, 4]
- P2: [6, 3, 8, 2] - [0, 1, 7, 1] = [6, 2, 1, 1]
- P3: [0, 5, 8, 0] - [0, 2, 2, 0] = [0, 3, 6, 0]

**Step 2 - apply the three tests of the resource-request algorithm**

- Test 1: Request [1, 0, 0, 2] vs Need [1, 0, 0, 3]: 1<=1, 0<=0, 0<=0, 2<=3 -> OK
- Test 2: Request [1, 0, 0, 2] vs Available [3, 5, 2, 4]: 1<=3, 0<=5, 0<=2, 2<=4 -> OK
- Test 3: pretend to grant. Available = [3, 5, 2, 4] - [1, 0, 0, 2] = [2, 5, 2, 2]; Allocation[P0] = [2, 2, 0, 5]. Now run the safety algorithm.
- Work = Available = [2, 5, 2, 2]
- P0: Need [0, 0, 0, 1] vs Work [2, 5, 2, 2]: 0<=2, 0<=5, 0<=2, 1<=2 -> all fit, run it. Work = [2, 5, 2, 2] + Allocation [2, 2, 0, 5] = [4, 7, 2, 7]
- P1: Need [1, 0, 1, 4] vs Work [4, 7, 2, 7]: 1<=4, 0<=7, 1<=2, 4<=7 -> all fit, run it. Work = [4, 7, 2, 7] + Allocation [2, 0, 0, 2] = [6, 7, 2, 9]
- P2: Need [6, 2, 1, 1] vs Work [6, 7, 2, 9]: 6<=6, 2<=7, 1<=2, 1<=9 -> all fit, run it. Work = [6, 7, 2, 9] + Allocation [0, 1, 7, 1] = [6, 8, 9, 10]
- P3: Need [0, 3, 6, 0] vs Work [6, 8, 9, 10]: 0<=6, 3<=8, 6<=9, 0<=10 -> all fit, run it. Work = [6, 8, 9, 10] + Allocation [0, 2, 2, 0] = [6, 10, 11, 10]
- SAFE. Safe sequence: < P0, P1, P2, P3 >
- Resulting state is SAFE (sequence < P0, P1, P2, P3 >) -> GRANT the request

**Conclusion: the request is GRANTED.**

**Answer: GRANTED**

problem:
A processor uses 4096-byte pages and the following page table: The page table is:

| Page | Frame |
|------|-------|
| 0    | 9     |
| 1    | 29    |
| 2    | 42    |
| 3    | 59    |

What physical address does logical address **12816** map to? Show your working.
solution:

- page offset = 12816 - 12288 = 528

- physical address = 241664 + 528 = 242192

**Answer: physical address = 242192**

problem:
A CI build agent uses a disk with cylinders 0-249. With the head at **27**, the following requests are pending:

`189, 149, 173, 3, 152, 49`

Using **SSTF** scheduling. List the order in which requests are served and compute the total distance moved.
solution:
**Policy: SSTF**

- at 27: nearest below 3 (27 - 3 = 24) vs above 49 (49 - 27 = 22); 22 < 24 -> 49
- at 49: nearest below 3 (49 - 3 = 46) vs above 149 (149 - 49 = 100); 46 < 100 -> 3
- at 3: only requests above remain; nearest above 149 (149 - 3 = 146) -> 149
- at 149: only requests above remain; nearest above 152 (152 - 149 = 3) -> 152
- at 152: only requests above remain; nearest above 173 (173 - 152 = 21) -> 173
- at 173: only requests above remain; nearest above 189 (189 - 173 = 16) -> 189
- 27 -> 49: 49 - 27 = 22; running total 0 + 22 = 22
- 49 -> 3: 49 - 3 = 46; running total 22 + 46 = 68
- 3 -> 149: 149 - 3 = 146; running total 68 + 146 = 214
- 149 -> 152: 152 - 149 = 3; running total 214 + 3 = 217
- 152 -> 173: 173 - 152 = 21; running total 217 + 21 = 238
- 173 -> 189: 189 - 173 = 16; running total 238 + 16 = 254

**Service order:** 49 -> 3 -> 149 -> 152 -> 173 -> 189
**Total head movement = 254 cylinders**
- Average seek length = 254 / 6 = 42.33

**Answer: total head movement = 254 cylinders**

problem: Memory partitions are 577 KB, 218 KB, 412 KB, 56 KB, 588 KB, in that order. The processes need 374 KB, 145 KB, 495 KB and 85 KB (in order). Using worst fit, show the allocation. Which processes cannot be allocated?
solution:
**Policy: WORST-fit**

_Rule: take the LARGEST hole that is large enough; the leftover stays as a smaller hole. A request that fits nowhere must wait._

- holes (free KB, numbered in order): hole 1=577, hole 2=218, hole 3=412, hole 4=56, hole 5=588
- request 374: hole 1=577 >= 374 fits; hole 2=218 < 374 no; hole 3=412 >= 374 fits; hole 4=56 < 374 no; hole 5=588 >= 374 fits -> largest fitting: 588 > 577 > 412 -> hole 5; 588 - 374 = 214
- request 145: hole 1=577 >= 145 fits; hole 2=218 >= 145 fits; hole 3=412 >= 145 fits; hole 4=56 < 145 no; hole 5=214 >= 145 fits -> largest fitting: 577 > 412 > 218 > 214 -> hole 1; 577 - 145 = 432
- request 495: hole 1=432 < 495 no; hole 2=218 < 495 no; hole 3=412 < 495 no; hole 4=56 < 495 no; hole 5=214 < 495 no -> no hole fits -> must WAIT
- request 85: hole 1=432 >= 85 fits; hole 2=218 >= 85 fits; hole 3=412 >= 85 fits; hole 4=56 < 85 no; hole 5=214 >= 85 fits -> largest fitting: 432 > 412 > 218 > 214 -> hole 1; 432 - 85 = 347

**Placement:** 374 KB -> hole 5; 145 KB -> hole 1; 495 KB -> WAIT; 85 KB -> hole 1
**Remaining free space per hole:** [347, 218, 412, 56, 214]
- Sum of free space: 347 + 218 = 565, 565 + 412 = 977, 977 + 56 = 1033, 1033 + 214 = 1247
**Total external fragmentation = 1247 KB**

**Answer: cannot be allocated: 495 KB**

| # | Ref | Result | Evicted | Why | Frames (least recently used first) | Faults |

| 2 | 4 | miss | - | free frame (2/3 used) | 0 4 | 2 |
| 3 | 5 | miss | - | free frame (3/3 used) | 0 4 5 | 3 |
| 4 | 1 | miss | 0 | frames full; last used 0@#1 < 4@#2 < 5@#3 -> least recent = 0 | 4 5 1 | 4 |
| 5 | 5 | hit | - | 5 already in frames | 4 1 5 | 4 |
| 6 | 1 | hit | - | 1 already in frames | 4 5 1 | 4 |
| 7 | 4 | hit | - | 4 already in frames | 5 1 4 | 4 |
| 8 | 4 | hit | - | 4 already in frames | 5 1 4 | 4 |
| 9 | 5 | hit | - | 5 already in frames | 1 4 5 | 4 |
| 10 | 2 | miss | 1 | frames full; last used 1@#6 < 4@#8 < 5@#9 -> least recent = 1 | 4 5 2 | 5 |
| 11 | 0 | miss | 4 | frames full; last used 4@#8 < 5@#9 < 2@#10 -> least recent = 4 | 5 2 0 | 6 |
| 12 | 3 | miss | 5 | frames full; last used 5@#9 < 2@#10 < 0@#11 -> least recent = 5 | 2 0 3 | 7 |
| 13 | 8 | miss | 2 | frames full; last used 2@#10 < 0@#11 < 3@#12 -> least recent = 2 | 0 3 8 | 8 |
| 14 | 3 | hit | - | 3 already in frames | 0 8 3 | 8 |
| 15 | 4 | miss | 0 | frames full; last used 0@#11 < 8@#13 < 3@#14 -> least recent = 0 | 8 3 4 | 9 |
| 16 | 0 | miss | 8 | frames full; last used 8@#13 < 3@#14 < 4@#15 -> least recent = 8 | 3 4 0 | 10 |
| 17 | 6 | miss | 3 | frames full; last used 3@#14 < 4@#15 < 0@#16 -> least recent = 3 | 4 0 6 | 11 |

**Total page faults = 11** (hits = 17 - 11 = 6, hit ratio = 6 / 17 = 0.3529, fault ratio = 11 / 17 = 0.6471)

problem:
You are analysing the workload of an air-traffic display system. The update tasks are:

| Process | Arrival | Burst |
|---------|---------|-------|
| P1      | 6       | 6     |
| P2      | 9       | 2     |
| P3      | 9       | 10    |
| P4      | 11      | 3     |
| P5      | 16      | 3     |

Assume **Round Robin (q=5)** scheduling with a time quantum of 5. Give the completion time of each process.
solution:
**Algorithm: Round Robin (q=5)**

**Step 1 - build the schedule**

_Rule: run the process at the HEAD of the queue for up to q = 5 units; processes arriving during a slice join the tail BEFORE the preempted process goes back to the tail._

- t=0: queue empty -> CPU idle until t=6
- t=6-11: run P1 (head of [P1]) for 5; 6 - 5 = 1 left; arrived P2(t=9), P3(t=9), P4(t=11) -> tail; P1 back to tail -> queue [P2, P3, P4, P1]
- t=11-13: run P2 (head of [P2, P3, P4, P1]) for 2; 2 - 2 = 0 left; P2 DONE at 13 -> queue [P3, P4, P1]
- t=13-18: run P3 (head of [P3, P4, P1]) for 5; 10 - 5 = 5 left; arrived P5(t=16) -> tail; P3 back to tail -> queue [P4, P1, P5, P3]
- t=18-21: run P4 (head of [P4, P1, P5, P3]) for 3; 3 - 3 = 0 left; P4 DONE at 21 -> queue [P1, P5, P3]
- t=21-22: run P1 (head of [P1, P5, P3]) for 1; 1 - 1 = 0 left; P1 DONE at 22 -> queue [P5, P3]
- t=22-25: run P5 (head of [P5, P3]) for 3; 3 - 3 = 0 left; P5 DONE at 25 -> queue [P3]
- t=25-30: run P3 (head of [P3]) for 5; 5 - 5 = 0 left; P3 DONE at 30 -> queue []

**Step 2 - Gantt chart:** P1[6-11] P2[11-13] P3[13-18] P4[18-21] P1[21-22] P5[22-25] P3[25-30]

**Step 3 - per-process times** (Turnaround = Completion - Arrival; Waiting = Turnaround - Burst)

| Process | Arrival | Burst | Completion | Turnaround   | Waiting      |
|---------|---------|-------|------------|--------------|--------------|
| P1      | 6       | 6     | 22         | 22 - 6 = 16  | 16 - 6 = 10  |
| P2      | 9       | 2     | 13         | 13 - 9 = 4   | 4 - 2 = 2    |
| P3      | 9       | 10    | 30         | 30 - 9 = 21  | 21 - 10 = 11 |
| P4      | 11      | 3     | 21         | 21 - 11 = 10 | 10 - 3 = 7   |
| P5      | 16      | 3     | 25         | 25 - 16 = 9  | 9 - 3 = 6    |

**Step 4 - averages**

- Sum of waiting times: 10 + 2 = 12, 12 + 11 = 23, 23 + 7 = 30, 30 + 6 = 36
- Average waiting time = 36 / 5 = **7.2**
- Sum of turnaround times: 16 + 4 = 20, 20 + 21 = 41, 41 + 10 = 51, 51 + 9 = 60
- Average turnaround time = 60 / 5 = **12.0**

**Answer: completion times P1 = 22, P2 = 13, P3 = 30, P4 = 21, P5 = 25**

- request 211: hole 1=545 >= 211 fits; hole 2=370 >= 211 fits; hole 3=541 >= 211 fits; hole 4=429 >= 211 fits -> smallest fitting: 370 < 429 < 541 < 545 -> hole 2; 370 - 211 = 159
- request 340: hole 1=545 >= 340 fits; hole 2=159 < 340 no; hole 3=541 >= 340 fits; hole 4=429 >= 340 fits -> smallest fitting: 429 < 541 < 545 -> hole 4; 429 - 340 = 89
- request 448: hole 1=545 >= 448 fits; hole 2=159 < 448 no; hole 3=541 >= 448 fits; hole 4=89 < 448 no -> smallest fitting: 541 < 545 -> hole 3; 541 - 448 = 93

problem:
The ready queue of an air-traffic display system contains:

P1 arrives at time 2 and requires 8 units of CPU time with priority 2; P2 arrives at time 2 and requires 12 units of CPU time with priority 3; P3 arrives at time 2 and requires 2 units of CPU time with priority 5; P4 arrives at time 4 and requires 5 units of CPU time with priority 2; P5 arrives at time 8 and requires 3 units of CPU time with priority 1; P6 arrives at time 9 and requires 10 units of CPU time with priority 2.

The scheduler uses **Priority (non-preemptive)** (a lower number means higher priority). Work through the schedule and give the average waiting time, showing all intermediate steps.
solution:
**Algorithm: Priority (non-preemptive)**

**Step 1 - build the schedule**

_Rule: whenever the CPU is free, run the ready process with the HIGHEST priority (LOWEST number) to completion (ties: earlier arrival, then name)._

- t=0: no process has arrived -> CPU idle until t=2
- t=2: ready P1(p2) < P2(p3) < P3(p5) -> run P1, done at 2 + 8 = 10
- t=10: ready P5(p1) < P4(p2) = P6(p2) < P2(p3) < P3(p5) -> run P5, done at 10 + 3 = 13
- t=13: ready P4(p2) = P6(p2) < P2(p3) < P3(p5) (tie -> earlier arrival, then name) -> run P4, done at 13 + 5 = 18
- t=18: ready P6(p2) < P2(p3) < P3(p5) -> run P6, done at 18 + 10 = 28
- t=28: ready P2(p3) < P3(p5) -> run P2, done at 28 + 12 = 40
- t=40: only P3 is ready -> run P3, done at 40 + 2 = 42

**Step 2 - Gantt chart:** P1[2-10] P5[10-13] P4[13-18] P6[18-28] P2[28-40] P3[40-42]

**Step 3 - per-process times** (Turnaround = Completion - Arrival; Waiting = Turnaround - Burst)

| Process | Arrival | Burst | Completion | Turnaround  | Waiting      |
|---------|---------|-------|------------|-------------|--------------|
| P1      | 2       | 8     | 10         | 10 - 2 = 8  | 8 - 8 = 0    |
| P2      | 2       | 12    | 40         | 40 - 2 = 38 | 38 - 12 = 26 |
| P3      | 2       | 2     | 42         | 42 - 2 = 40 | 40 - 2 = 38  |

problem:
Q. The available vector is (5,2,3).

| Process | Alloc A | Alloc B | Alloc C | Max A | Max B | Max C |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| P0 | 0 | 3 | 0 | 8 | 8 | 0 |
| P1 | 2 | 0 | 3 | 5 | 2 | 7 |
| P2 | 5 | 1 | 2 | 7 | 8 | 4 |
| P3 | 5 | 3 | 0 | 6 | 5 | 2 |

If P0 makes a request (4, 0, 0), should it be granted?
solution:
**Step 1 - compute Need = Max - Allocation, row by row** (resources A, B, C)

- P0: [8, 8, 0] - [0, 3, 0] = [8, 5, 0]
- P1: [5, 2, 7] - [2, 0, 3] = [3, 2, 4]
- P2: [7, 8, 4] - [5, 1, 2] = [2, 7, 2]
- P3: [6, 5, 2] - [5, 3, 0] = [1, 2, 2]

**Step 2 - apply the three tests of the resource-request algorithm**

- Test 1: Request [4, 0, 0] vs Need [8, 5, 0]: 4<=8, 0<=5, 0<=0 -> OK
- Test 2: Request [4, 0, 0] vs Available [5, 2, 3]: 4<=5, 0<=2, 0<=3 -> OK
- Test 3: pretend to grant. Available = [5, 2, 3] - [4, 0, 0] = [1, 2, 3]; Allocation[P0] = [4, 3, 0]. Now run the safety algorithm.
- Work = Available = [1, 2, 3]
- P0: Need [4, 5, 0] vs Work [1, 2, 3]: 4>1, 5>2, 0<=3 -> cannot run yet
- P1: Need [3, 2, 4] vs Work [1, 2, 3]: 3>1, 2<=2, 4>3 -> cannot run yet
- P2: Need [2, 7, 2] vs Work [1, 2, 3]: 2>1, 7>2, 2<=3 -> cannot run yet
- P3: Need [1, 2, 2] vs Work [1, 2, 3]: 1<=1, 2<=2, 2<=3 -> all fit, run it. Work = [1, 2, 3] + Allocation [5, 3, 0] = [6, 5, 3]
- P0: Need [4, 5, 0] vs Work [6, 5, 3]: 4<=6, 5<=5, 0<=3 -> all fit, run it. Work = [6, 5, 3] + Allocation [4, 3, 0] = [10, 8, 3]
- P1: Need [3, 2, 4] vs Work [10, 8, 3]: 3<=10, 2<=8, 4>3 -> cannot run yet
- P2: Need [2, 7, 2] vs Work [10, 8, 3]: 2<=10, 7<=8, 2<=3 -> all fit, run it. Work = [10, 8, 3] + Allocation [5, 1, 2] = [15, 9, 5]
- P1: Need [3, 2, 4] vs Work [15, 9, 5]: 3<=15, 2<=9, 4<=5 -> all fit, run it. Work = [15, 9, 5] + Allocation [2, 0, 3] = [17, 9, 8]
- SAFE. Safe sequence: < P3, P0, P2, P1 >
- Resulting state is SAFE (sequence < P3, P0, P2, P1 >) -> GRANT the request

**Conclusion: the request is GRANTED.**

**Answer: GRANTED**

problem:
A memory manager tracks these free blocks (KB, in address order): `[515, 350, 64, 492, 425]`. Processes request `[296, 388, 348, 88]` KB, in that order.

Allocate these requests with **WORST-fit** and report the leftover space in each hole.
solution:
**Policy: WORST-fit**

_Rule: take the LARGEST hole that is large enough; the leftover stays as a smaller hole. A request that fits nowhere must wait._

- holes (free KB, numbered in order): hole 1=515, hole 2=350, hole 3=64, hole 4=492, hole 5=425
- request 296: hole 1=515 >= 296 fits; hole 2=350 >= 296 fits; hole 3=64 < 296 no; hole 4=492 >= 296 fits; hole 5=425 >= 296 fits -> largest fitting: 515 > 492 > 425 > 350 -> hole 1; 515 - 296 = 219
- request 388: hole 1=219 < 388 no; hole 2=350 < 388 no; hole 3=64 < 388 no; hole 4=492 >= 388 fits; hole 5=425 >= 388 fits -> largest fitting: 492 > 425 -> hole 4; 492 - 388 = 104
- request 348: hole 1=219 < 348 no; hole 2=350 >= 348 fits; hole 3=64 < 348 no; hole 4=104 < 348 no; hole 5=425 >= 348 fits -> largest fitting: 425 > 350 -> hole 5; 425 - 348 = 77
- request 88: hole 1=219 >= 88 fits; hole 2=350 >= 88 fits; hole 3=64 < 88 no; hole 4=104 >= 88 fits; hole 5=77 < 88 no -> largest fitting: 350 > 219 > 104 -> hole 2; 350 - 88 = 262

**Placement:** 296 KB -> hole 1; 388 KB -> hole 4; 348 KB -> hole 5; 88 KB -> hole 2
**Remaining free space per hole:** [219, 262, 64, 104, 77]
- Sum of free space: 219 + 262 = 481, 481 + 64 = 545, 545 + 104 = 649, 649 + 77 = 726
**Total external fragmentation = 726 KB**

**Answer: 296 KB -> hole 1; 388 KB -> hole 4; 348 KB -> hole 5; 88 KB -> hole 2**

problem: I need help with this problem. Assume a page size of 2048 bytes. The page table maps page 0 -> frame 55, page 1 -> frame 61, page 2 -> frame 58, page 3 -> frame 34, page 4 -> frame 40, page 5 -> frame 60. Find the physical address for virtual address 0x26f2.
solution:
**Step-by-step translation**

- convert 0x26f2 to decimal: 2 x 4096 = 8192; 6 x 256 = 1536; 15 x 16 = 240; 2 x 1 = 2
- sum: 8192 + 1536 = 9728, 9728 + 240 = 9968, 9968 + 2 = 9970 -> 0x26f2 = 9970
- page number = floor(9970 / 2048) = 4  (check: 4 x 2048 = 8192 <= 9970 < 10240)
- page offset = 9970 - 8192 = 1778
- page table[4] = frame 40
- frame base = 40 x 2048 = 81920
- physical address = 81920 + 1778 = 83698

**Physical address = 83698**
- in hexadecimal: 83698 = 0x146f2

**Answer: physical address = 83698 (0x146f2)**

problem:

- P1: Need [2, 3, 2, 4] vs Work [3, 6, 3, 2]: 2<=3, 3<=6, 2<=3, 4>2 -> cannot run yet
- P2: Need [1, 0, 5, 0] vs Work [3, 6, 3, 2]: 1<=3, 0<=6, 5>3, 0<=2 -> cannot run yet

- P4: Need [0, 1, 2, 2] vs Work [3, 6, 3, 2]: 0<=3, 1<=6, 2<=3, 2<=2 -> all fit, run it. Work = [3, 6, 3, 2] + Allocation [0, 3, 1, 5] = [3, 9, 4, 7]

problem: Q. Processes A, B, C, D, E have arrival times 0, 2, 3, 4, 5 and burst times 2, 2, 12, 10, 2 ms, with priorities 5, 3, 2, 5, 4 respectively. Apply priority scheduling with preemption. When does each process finish? (lower value = higher priority)
solution:
**Algorithm: Priority (preemptive)**

**Step 1 - build the schedule**

_Rule: at every arrival and completion, run the ready process with the HIGHEST priority (LOWEST number); preempt the running process if a higher-priority one is ready (ties: earlier arrival, then name)._

- t=0: A arrives; only A is ready -> run A
- t=2: A completes; B arrives; only B is ready -> run B
- t=3: C arrives; ready C(p2) < B(p3) -> PREEMPT B, run C
- t=4: D arrives; ready C(p2) < B(p3) < D(p5) -> keep running C
- t=5: E arrives; ready C(p2) < B(p3) < E(p4) < D(p5) -> keep running C
- t=15: C completes; ready B(p3) < E(p4) < D(p5) -> run B
- t=16: B completes; ready E(p4) < D(p5) -> run E
- t=18: E completes; only D is ready -> run D
- t=28: D completes; all processes done

**Step 2 - Gantt chart:** A[0-2] B[2-3] C[3-15] B[15-16] E[16-18] D[18-28]

**Step 3 - per-process times** (Turnaround = Completion - Arrival; Waiting = Turnaround - Burst)

| Process | Arrival | Burst | Completion | Turnaround  | Waiting      |
|---------|---------|-------|------------|-------------|--------------|
| A       | 0       | 2     | 2          | 2 - 0 = 2   | 2 - 2 = 0    |
| B       | 2       | 2     | 16         | 16 - 2 = 14 | 14 - 2 = 12  |
| C       | 3       | 12    | 15         | 15 - 3 = 12 | 12 - 12 = 0  |
| D       | 4       | 10    | 28         | 28 - 4 = 24 | 24 - 10 = 14 |
| E       | 5       | 2     | 18         | 18 - 5 = 13 | 13 - 2 = 11  |

**Step 4 - averages**

- Sum of waiting times: 0 + 12 = 12, 12 + 0 = 12, 12 + 14 = 26, 26 + 11 = 37
- Average waiting time = 37 / 5 = **7.4**
- Sum of turnaround times: 2 + 14 = 16, 16 + 12 = 28, 28 + 24 = 52, 52 + 13 = 65
- Average turnaround time = 65 / 5 = **13.0**

**Answer: completion times A = 2, B = 16, C = 15, D = 28, E = 18**

problem: Consider the following. Head position: 95. Requests arrive for cylinders 178, 119, 118, 179, 20, 138, 201, 34, 185. The arm is moving towards 249. Using C-LOOK scheduling, calculate the total seek distance.

problem:
The resource allocation state of a system with 4 resource types (A, B, C, D) is: Available = [3, 5, 3, 4].

| P | Alloc A | Alloc B | Alloc C | Alloc D | Max A | Max B | Max C | Max D |
|---|---------|---------|---------|---------|-------|-------|-------|-------|
| A | 1       | 0       | 2       | 4       | 2     | 4     | 2     | 7     |
| B | 0       | 0       | 0       | 3       | 3     | 1     | 0     | 5     |
| C | 5       | 1       | 1       | 1       | 5     | 4     | 1     | 5     |
| D | 3       | 3       | 3       | 0       | 7     | 3     | 6     | 0     |
| E | 2       | 0       | 6       | 8       | 8     | 1     | 8     | 8     |

A request of [2, 0, 2, 0] arrives from D. Can it be satisfied safely?
solution:
**Step 1 - compute Need = Max - Allocation, row by row** (resources A, B, C, D)

- A: [2, 4, 2, 7] - [1, 0, 2, 4] = [1, 4, 0, 3]
- B: [3, 1, 0, 5] - [0, 0, 0, 3] = [3, 1, 0, 2]
- C: [5, 4, 1, 5] - [5, 1, 1, 1] = [0, 3, 0, 4]
- D: [7, 3, 6, 0] - [3, 3, 3, 0] = [4, 0, 3, 0]
- E: [8, 1, 8, 8] - [2, 0, 6, 8] = [6, 1, 2, 0]

**Step 2 - apply the three tests of the resource-request algorithm**

- Test 1: Request [2, 0, 2, 0] vs Need [4, 0, 3, 0]: 2<=4, 0<=0, 2<=3, 0<=0 -> OK
- Test 2: Request [2, 0, 2, 0] vs Available [3, 5, 3, 4]: 2<=3, 0<=5, 2<=3, 0<=4 -> OK
- Test 3: pretend to grant. Available = [3, 5, 3, 4] - [2, 0, 2, 0] = [1, 5, 1, 4]; Allocation[D] = [5, 3, 5, 0]. Now run the safety algorithm.
- Work = Available = [1, 5, 1, 4]
- A: Need [1, 4, 0, 3] vs Work [1, 5, 1, 4]: 1<=1, 4<=5, 0<=1, 3<=4 -> all fit, run it. Work = [1, 5, 1, 4] + Allocation [1, 0, 2, 4] = [2, 5, 3, 8]
- B: Need [3, 1, 0, 2] vs Work [2, 5, 3, 8]: 3>2, 1<=5, 0<=3, 2<=8 -> cannot run yet
- C: Need [0, 3, 0, 4] vs Work [2, 5, 3, 8]: 0<=2, 3<=5, 0<=3, 4<=8 -> all fit, run it. Work = [2, 5, 3, 8] + Allocation [5, 1, 1, 1] = [7, 6, 4, 9]
- B: Need [3, 1, 0, 2] vs Work [7, 6, 4, 9]: 3<=7, 1<=6, 0<=4, 2<=9 -> all fit, run it. Work = [7, 6, 4, 9] + Allocation [0, 0, 0, 3] = [7, 6, 4, 12]
- D: Need [2, 0, 1, 0] vs Work [7, 6, 4, 12]: 2<=7, 0<=6, 1<=4, 0<=12 -> all fit, run it. Work = [7, 6, 4, 12] + Allocation [5, 3, 5, 0] = [12, 9, 9, 12]
- E: Need [6, 1, 2, 0] vs Work [12, 9, 9, 12]: 6<=12, 1<=9, 2<=9, 0<=12 -> all fit, run it. Work = [12, 9, 9, 12] + Allocation [2, 0, 6, 8] = [14, 9, 15, 20]
- SAFE. Safe sequence: < A, C, B, D, E >
- Resulting state is SAFE (sequence < A, C, B, D, E >) -> GRANT the request

**Conclusion: the request is GRANTED.**

**Answer: GRANTED**

| 7 | 2 | hit | - | 2 already in frames | 2 5 8 3 | 5 |

problem: Q. The total instances of A, B, C, D are <8, 6, 29, 16>. Allocation = [[0, 2, 6, 5], [1, 1, 4, 7], [1, 0, 6, 1], [3, 0, 7, 1]]. Max = [[0, 2, 6, 8], [2, 4, 8, 8], [3, 0, 6, 1], [3, 2, 7, 1]]. Use the Banker's algorithm to check whether the state is safe.
solution:
**Step 0 - Available = Total - (sum of each Allocation column)**

- A: allocated 0 + 1 = 1, 1 + 1 = 2, 2 + 3 = 5; available 8 - 5 = 3
- B: allocated 2 + 1 = 3, 3 + 0 = 3, 3 + 0 = 3; available 6 - 3 = 3
- C: allocated 6 + 4 = 10, 10 + 6 = 16, 16 + 7 = 23; available 29 - 23 = 6
- D: allocated 5 + 7 = 12, 12 + 1 = 13, 13 + 1 = 14; available 16 - 14 = 2
- Available = [3, 3, 6, 2]

**Step 1 - compute Need = Max - Allocation, row by row** (resources A, B, C, D)

- 3145: [0, 2, 6, 8] - [0, 2, 6, 5] = [0, 0, 0, 3]
- 3157: [2, 4, 8, 8] - [1, 1, 4, 7] = [1, 3, 4, 1]
- 3167: [3, 0, 6, 1] - [1, 0, 6, 1] = [2, 0, 0, 0]
- 3182: [3, 2, 7, 1] - [3, 0, 7, 1] = [0, 2, 0, 0]

**Step 2 - run the safety algorithm** (scan the processes in order; run the first one whose Need fits in Work, then add its Allocation to Work and scan again)

- Work = Available = [3, 3, 6, 2]
- 3145: Need [0, 0, 0, 3] vs Work [3, 3, 6, 2]: 0<=3, 0<=3, 0<=6, 3>2 -> cannot run yet
- 3157: Need [1, 3, 4, 1] vs Work [3, 3, 6, 2]: 1<=3, 3<=3, 4<=6, 1<=2 -> all fit, run it. Work = [3, 3, 6, 2] + Allocation [1, 1, 4, 7] = [4, 4, 10, 9]
- 3145: Need [0, 0, 0, 3] vs Work [4, 4, 10, 9]: 0<=4, 0<=4, 0<=10, 3<=9 -> all fit, run it. Work = [4, 4, 10, 9] + Allocation [0, 2, 6, 5] = [4, 6, 16, 14]
- 3167: Need [2, 0, 0, 0] vs Work [4, 6, 16, 14]: 2<=4, 0<=6, 0<=16, 0<=14 -> all fit, run it. Work = [4, 6, 16, 14] + Allocation [1, 0, 6, 1] = [5, 6, 22, 15]
- 3182: Need [0, 2, 0, 0] vs Work [5, 6, 22, 15]: 0<=5, 2<=6, 0<=22, 0<=15 -> all fit, run it. Work = [5, 6, 22, 15] + Allocation [3, 0, 7, 1] = [8, 6, 29, 16]

**Step 3 - conclusion**

All 4 processes can complete, so the system is in a **SAFE state**.
A safe sequence is **< 3157, 3145, 3167, 3182 >**.

_Safe sequences are not unique: any ordering in which each process's Need is met by the running Work vector is equally correct._

**Answer: SAFE, safe sequence < 3157, 3145, 3167, 3182 >**

problem:

Using **LOOK** scheduling. The head is currently moving toward lower cylinder numbers. Give the service order and the total head movement.
solution:
**Policy: LOOK**

- sorted requests: [3, 8, 83, 110, 127, 194]; below head 136: [3, 8, 83, 110, 127]; at/above head: [194]
- LOOK, head moving DOWN, towards cylinder 0: service [127, 110, 83, 8, 3], reverse at the last request (not the edge), then service [194]
- 136 -> 127: 136 - 127 = 9; running total 0 + 9 = 9
- 127 -> 110: 127 - 110 = 17; running total 9 + 17 = 26
- 110 -> 83: 110 - 83 = 27; running total 26 + 27 = 53
- 83 -> 8: 83 - 8 = 75; running total 53 + 75 = 128
- 8 -> 3: 8 - 3 = 5; running total 128 + 5 = 133
- 3 -> 194: 194 - 3 = 191; running total 133 + 191 = 324

**Service order:** 127 -> 110 -> 83 -> 8 -> 3 -> 194
**Total head movement = 324 cylinders**
- Average seek length = 324 / 6 = 54.0

**Answer: total head movement = 324 cylinders**

problem:
The resource allocation state of a system with 4 resource types (A, B, C, D) is: The system has [1, 0, 5, 4] instances of each type free.

| P1 | 2       | 2       | 0       | 0       | 5     | 5     | 0     | 3     |
| P2 | 1       | 1       | 3       | 0       | 4     | 2     | 4     | 0     |
| P3 | 2       | 0       | 0       | 1       | 6     | 6     | 0     | 1     |

Is this state safe? Apply the safety algorithm and show a safe sequence if one exists.
solution:
**Step 1 - compute Need = Max - Allocation, row by row** (resources A, B, C, D)

- P0: [4, 0, 3, 5] - [1, 0, 1, 0] = [3, 0, 2, 5]
- P1: [5, 5, 0, 3] - [2, 2, 0, 0] = [3, 3, 0, 3]
- P2: [4, 2, 4, 0] - [1, 1, 3, 0] = [3, 1, 1, 0]
- P3: [6, 6, 0, 1] - [2, 0, 0, 1] = [4, 6, 0, 0]

**Step 2 - run the safety algorithm** (scan the processes in order; run the first one whose Need fits in Work, then add its Allocation to Work and scan again)

- Work = Available = [1, 0, 5, 4]
- P0: Need [3, 0, 2, 5] vs Work [1, 0, 5, 4]: 3>1, 0<=0, 2<=5, 5>4 -> cannot run yet
- P1: Need [3, 3, 0, 3] vs Work [1, 0, 5, 4]: 3>1, 3>0, 0<=5, 3<=4 -> cannot run yet

problem:
Memory contains holes of sizes `[543, 183, 67, 265, 488]` (in KB, in this order). Requests arrive for `[278, 462, 474]` KB in order.

Apply **WORST-fit** allocation. Which partition serves each request?
solution:
**Policy: WORST-fit**

_Rule: take the LARGEST hole that is large enough; the leftover stays as a smaller hole. A request that fits nowhere must wait._

- holes (free KB, numbered in order): hole 1=543, hole 2=183, hole 3=67, hole 4=265, hole 5=488
- request 278: hole 1=543 >= 278 fits; hole 2=183 < 278 no; hole 3=67 < 278 no; hole 4=265 < 278 no; hole 5=488 >= 278 fits -> largest fitting: 543 > 488 -> hole 1; 543 - 278 = 265
- request 462: hole 1=265 < 462 no; hole 2=183 < 462 no; hole 3=67 < 462 no; hole 4=265 < 462 no; hole 5=488 >= 462 fits -> largest fitting: 488 -> hole 5; 488 - 462 = 26
- request 474: hole 1=265 < 474 no; hole 2=183 < 474 no; hole 3=67 < 474 no; hole 4=265 < 474 no; hole 5=26 < 474 no -> no hole fits -> must WAIT

**Placement:** 278 KB -> hole 1; 462 KB -> hole 5; 474 KB -> WAIT
**Remaining free space per hole:** [265, 183, 67, 265, 26]
- Sum of free space: 265 + 183 = 448, 448 + 67 = 515, 515 + 265 = 780, 780 + 26 = 806
**Total external fragmentation = 806 KB**

**Answer: 278 KB -> hole 1; 462 KB -> hole 5; 474 KB -> WAIT**

- Test 3: pretend to grant. Available = [5, 5, 6] - [0, 1, 0] = [5, 4, 6]; Allocation[P0] = [2, 2, 0]. Now run the safety algorithm.
- Work = Available = [5, 4, 6]
- P0: Need [2, 1, 0] vs Work [5, 4, 6]: 2<=5, 1<=4, 0<=6 -> all fit, run it. Work = [5, 4, 6] + Allocation [2, 2, 0] = [7, 6, 6]
- P1: Need [1, 4, 1] vs Work [7, 6, 6]: 1<=7, 4<=6, 1<=6 -> all fit, run it. Work = [7, 6, 6] + Allocation [3, 1, 7] = [10, 7, 13]
- P2: Need [0, 3, 0] vs Work [10, 7, 13]: 0<=10, 3<=7, 0<=13 -> all fit, run it. Work = [10, 7, 13] + Allocation [2, 1, 1] = [12, 8, 14]
- P3: Need [2, 4, 1] vs Work [12, 8, 14]: 2<=12, 4<=8, 1<=14 -> all fit, run it. Work = [12, 8, 14] + Allocation [3, 0, 4] = [15, 8, 18]
- SAFE. Safe sequence: < P0, P1, P2, P3 >
- Resulting state is SAFE (sequence < P0, P1, P2, P3 >) -> GRANT the request

**Conclusion: the request is GRANTED.**

**Answer: GRANTED**

problem:
A memory manager tracks these free blocks (KB, in address order): `[467, 239, 160, 199]`. The following allocations are requested in sequence: `[399, 391, 169, 473]` KB.

Apply **FIRST-fit** allocation. Which partition serves each request?
solution:
**Policy: FIRST-fit**

_Rule: scan holes in order and take the FIRST that is large enough; the leftover stays as a smaller hole. A request that fits nowhere must wait._

- holes (free KB, numbered in order): hole 1=467, hole 2=239, hole 3=160, hole 4=199
- request 399: hole 1=467 >= 399 fits -> first fitting hole = hole 1; 467 - 399 = 68
- request 391: hole 1=68 < 391 no; hole 2=239 < 391 no; hole 3=160 < 391 no; hole 4=199 < 391 no -> no hole fits -> must WAIT
- request 169: hole 1=68 < 169 no; hole 2=239 >= 169 fits -> first fitting hole = hole 2; 239 - 169 = 70
- request 473: hole 1=68 < 473 no; hole 2=70 < 473 no; hole 3=160 < 473 no; hole 4=199 < 473 no -> no hole fits -> must WAIT

**Placement:** 399 KB -> hole 1; 391 KB -> WAIT; 169 KB -> hole 2; 473 KB -> WAIT
**Remaining free space per hole:** [68, 70, 160, 199]
- Sum of free space: 68 + 70 = 138, 138 + 160 = 298, 298 + 199 = 497
**Total external fragmentation = 497 KB**

**Answer: 399 KB -> hole 1; 391 KB -> WAIT; 169 KB -> hole 2; 473 KB -> WAIT**

problem:
Consider the following. Currently available: A=1, B=2, C=2, D=4.

| Process | Alloc A | Alloc B | Alloc C | Alloc D | Max A | Max B | Max C | Max D |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| J1 | 4 | 0 | 2 | 0 | 4 | 0 | 3 | 1 |
| J2 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 2 | 3 | 5 | 0 | 3 |
| J3 | 0 | 5 | 0 | 0 | 3 | 6 | 1 | 2 |
| J4 | 3 | 5 | 7 | 8 | 4 | 6 | 7 | 8 |

J1 requests (0,0,1,0). Can the request be granted immediately?
solution:
**Step 1 - compute Need = Max - Allocation, row by row** (resources A, B, C, D)

- J1: [4, 0, 3, 1] - [4, 0, 2, 0] = [0, 0, 1, 1]
- J2: [3, 5, 0, 3] - [0, 0, 0, 2] = [3, 5, 0, 1]
- J3: [3, 6, 1, 2] - [0, 5, 0, 0] = [3, 1, 1, 2]
- J4: [4, 6, 7, 8] - [3, 5, 7, 8] = [1, 1, 0, 0]

**Step 2 - apply the three tests of the resource-request algorithm**

- Test 1: Request [0, 0, 1, 0] vs Need [0, 0, 1, 1]: 0<=0, 0<=0, 1<=1, 0<=1 -> OK
- Test 2: Request [0, 0, 1, 0] vs Available [1, 2, 2, 4]: 0<=1, 0<=2, 1<=2, 0<=4 -> OK
- Test 3: pretend to grant. Available = [1, 2, 2, 4] - [0, 0, 1, 0] = [1, 2, 1, 4]; Allocation[J1] = [4, 0, 3, 0]. Now run the safety algorithm.
- Work = Available = [1, 2, 1, 4]
- J1: Need [0, 0, 0, 1] vs Work [1, 2, 1, 4]: 0<=1, 0<=2, 0<=1, 1<=4 -> all fit, run it. Work = [1, 2, 1, 4] + Allocation [4, 0, 3, 0] = [5, 2, 4, 4]
- J2: Need [3, 5, 0, 1] vs Work [5, 2, 4, 4]: 3<=5, 5>2, 0<=4, 1<=4 -> cannot run yet
- J3: Need [3, 1, 1, 2] vs Work [5, 2, 4, 4]: 3<=5, 1<=2, 1<=4, 2<=4 -> all fit, run it. Work = [5, 2, 4, 4] + Allocation [0, 5, 0, 0] = [5, 7, 4, 4]
- J2: Need [3, 5, 0, 1] vs Work [5, 7, 4, 4]: 3<=5, 5<=7, 0<=4, 1<=4 -> all fit, run it. Work = [5, 7, 4, 4] + Allocation [0, 0, 0, 2] = [5, 7, 4, 6]
- J4: Need [1, 1, 0, 0] vs Work [5, 7, 4, 6]: 1<=5, 1<=7, 0<=4, 0<=6 -> all fit, run it. Work = [5, 7, 4, 6] + Allocation [3, 5, 7, 8] = [8, 12, 11, 14]
- SAFE. Safe sequence: < J1, J3, J2, J4 >
- Resulting state is SAFE (sequence < J1, J3, J2, J4 >) -> GRANT the request

**Conclusion: the request is GRANTED.**

problem:
A database server has free memory partitions of `[520, 569, 69, 100, 227, 101]` KB. Requests arrive for `[216, 295, 105, 161, 492]` KB in order.

Apply **WORST-fit** allocation. Which partition serves each request?
solution:
**Policy: WORST-fit**

_Rule: take the LARGEST hole that is large enough; the leftover stays as a smaller hole. A request that fits nowhere must wait._

- holes (free KB, numbered in order): hole 1=520, hole 2=569, hole 3=69, hole 4=100, hole 5=227, hole 6=101
- request 216: hole 1=520 >= 216 fits; hole 2=569 >= 216 fits; hole 3=69 < 216 no; hole 4=100 < 216 no; hole 5=227 >= 216 fits; hole 6=101 < 216 no -> largest fitting: 569 > 520 > 227 -> hole 2; 569 - 216 = 353
- request 295: hole 1=520 >= 295 fits; hole 2=353 >= 295 fits; hole 3=69 < 295 no; hole 4=100 < 295 no; hole 5=227 < 295 no; hole 6=101 < 295 no -> largest fitting: 520 > 353 -> hole 1; 520 - 295 = 225
- request 105: hole 1=225 >= 105 fits; hole 2=353 >= 105 fits; hole 3=69 < 105 no; hole 4=100 < 105 no; hole 5=227 >= 105 fits; hole 6=101 < 105 no -> largest fitting: 353 > 227 > 225 -> hole 2; 353 - 105 = 248
- request 161: hole 1=225 >= 161 fits; hole 2=248 >= 161 fits; hole 3=69 < 161 no; hole 4=100 < 161 no; hole 5=227 >= 161 fits; hole 6=101 < 161 no -> largest fitting: 248 > 227 > 225 -> hole 2; 248 - 161 = 87
- request 492: hole 1=225 < 492 no; hole 2=87 < 492 no; hole 3=69 < 492 no; hole 4=100 < 492 no; hole 5=227 < 492 no; hole 6=101 < 492 no -> no hole fits -> must WAIT

**Placement:** 216 KB -> hole 2; 295 KB -> hole 1; 105 KB -> hole 2; 161 KB -> hole 2; 492 KB -> WAIT
**Remaining free space per hole:** [225, 87, 69, 100, 227, 101]
- Sum of free space: 225 + 87 = 312, 312 + 69 = 381, 381 + 100 = 481, 481 + 227 = 708, 708 + 101 = 809
**Total external fragmentation = 809 KB**

**Answer: 216 KB -> hole 2; 295 KB -> hole 1; 105 KB -> hole 2; 161 KB -> hole 2; 492 KB -> WAIT**

problem: Consider the following. Processes (arrival, burst): P1 (2, 3), P2 (2, 3), P3 (2, 6), P4 (2, 1), P5 (4, 3). Using first-come, first-served (FCFS), when does each process finish?
solution:
**Algorithm: FCFS**

**Step 1 - build the schedule**

_Rule: run processes in order of ARRIVAL; each runs to completion._

- arrival order: P1(t=2), P2(t=2), P3(t=2), P4(t=2), P5(t=4)
- t=0: no process has arrived -> CPU idle until t=2
- t=2: P1 runs (arrived t=2, burst 3) -> completes at 2 + 3 = 5
- t=5: P2 runs (arrived t=2, burst 3) -> completes at 5 + 3 = 8
- t=8: P3 runs (arrived t=2, burst 6) -> completes at 8 + 6 = 14
- t=14: P4 runs (arrived t=2, burst 1) -> completes at 14 + 1 = 15
- t=15: P5 runs (arrived t=4, burst 3) -> completes at 15 + 3 = 18

**Step 2 - Gantt chart:** P1[2-5] P2[5-8] P3[8-14] P4[14-15] P5[15-18]

**Step 3 - per-process times** (Turnaround = Completion - Arrival; Waiting = Turnaround - Burst)

| Process | Arrival | Burst | Completion | Turnaround  | Waiting     |
|---------|---------|-------|------------|-------------|-------------|
| P1      | 2       | 3     | 5          | 5 - 2 = 3   | 3 - 3 = 0   |
| P2      | 2       | 3     | 8          | 8 - 2 = 6   | 6 - 3 = 3   |
| P3      | 2       | 6     | 14         | 14 - 2 = 12 | 12 - 6 = 6  |
| P4      | 2       | 1     | 15         | 15 - 2 = 13 | 13 - 1 = 12 |
| P5      | 4       | 3     | 18         | 18 - 4 = 14 | 14 - 3 = 11 |

**Step 4 - averages**

- Sum of waiting times: 0 + 3 = 3, 3 + 6 = 9, 9 + 12 = 21, 21 + 11 = 32
- Average waiting time = 32 / 5 = **6.4**
- Sum of turnaround times: 3 + 6 = 9, 9 + 12 = 21, 21 + 13 = 34, 34 + 14 = 48
- Average turnaround time = 48 / 5 = **9.6**

**Answer: completion times P1 = 5, P2 = 8, P3 = 14, P4 = 15, P5 = 18**

problem: P1 arrives at time 5 and has a burst of 2 ms; P2 arrives at 11 and needs 7 ms; P3 arrives at 14 and has a burst of 5 ms; P4 arrives at 16 and has a burst of 8 ms; P5 arrives at 16 and needs 1 ms. The scheduler uses highest response ratio next scheduling. Compute the average waiting and turnaround times.
solution:
**Algorithm: HRRN (highest response ratio next)**

**Step 1 - build the schedule**

_Rule: whenever the CPU is free, compute each ready process's response ratio = (waiting + burst) / burst and run the HIGHEST ratio to completion (ties: earlier arrival, then name)._

- t=0: no process has arrived -> CPU idle until t=5
- t=5: only P1 is ready -> run P1, done at 5 + 2 = 7
- t=7: no process has arrived -> CPU idle until t=11
- t=11: only P2 is ready -> run P2, done at 11 + 7 = 18
- t=18: ratios: P3 waited 18 - 14 = 4, (4 + 5) / 5 = 1.80, P4 waited 18 - 16 = 2, (2 + 8) / 8 = 1.25, P5 waited 18 - 16 = 2, (2 + 1) / 1 = 3.00; order P5(3.00) > P3(1.80) > P4(1.25) -> run P5, done at 18 + 1 = 19
- t=19: ratios: P3 waited 19 - 14 = 5, (5 + 5) / 5 = 2.00, P4 waited 19 - 16 = 3, (3 + 8) / 8 = 1.38; order P3(2.00) > P4(1.38) -> run P3, done at 19 + 5 = 24
- t=24: only P4 is ready -> run P4, done at 24 + 8 = 32

**Step 2 - Gantt chart:** P1[5-7] P2[11-18] P5[18-19] P3[19-24] P4[24-32]

**Step 3 - per-process times** (Turnaround = Completion - Arrival; Waiting = Turnaround - Burst)

| Process | Arrival | Burst | Completion | Turnaround   | Waiting    |
|---------|---------|-------|------------|--------------|------------|
| P1      | 5       | 2     | 7          | 7 - 5 = 2    | 2 - 2 = 0  |
| P2      | 11      | 7     | 18         | 18 - 11 = 7  | 7 - 7 = 0  |
| P3      | 14      | 5     | 24         | 24 - 14 = 10 | 10 - 5 = 5 |
| P4      | 16      | 8     | 32         | 32 - 16 = 16 | 16 - 8 = 8 |
| P5      | 16      | 1     | 19         | 19 - 16 = 3  | 3 - 1 = 2  |

**Step 4 - averages**

- Sum of waiting times: 0 + 0 = 0, 0 + 5 = 5, 5 + 8 = 13, 13 + 2 = 15
- Average waiting time = 15 / 5 = **3.0**
- Sum of turnaround times: 2 + 7 = 9, 9 + 10 = 19, 19 + 16 = 35, 35 + 3 = 38
- Average turnaround time = 38 / 5 = **7.6**

**Answer: average waiting time = 3.0, average turnaround time = 7.6**

problem:
A process generates the following sequence of page references:

`4 1 6 1 2 2 4 7 6 1 2 0 6 0 2 3 4 7 2 4`

and the process is allocated **4 page frames**, using the **OPT** replacement policy. How many page faults occur? Show the frame contents after each reference.
solution:
**Policy: OPT, 4 frames** (all empty at the start)

_Rule: on a fault with all frames full, evict the page whose NEXT USE is FARTHEST in the future (never used again = farthest)._

| # | Ref | Result | Evicted | Why | Frames (frame order) | Faults |
|---|-----|--------|---------|-----|--------|--------|
| 1 | 4 | miss | - | free frame (1/4 used) | 4 | 1 |
| 2 | 1 | miss | - | free frame (2/4 used) | 4 1 | 2 |
| 3 | 6 | miss | - | free frame (3/4 used) | 4 1 6 | 3 |
| 4 | 1 | hit | - | 1 already in frames | 4 1 6 | 3 |
| 5 | 2 | miss | - | free frame (4/4 used) | 4 1 6 2 | 4 |
| 6 | 2 | hit | - | 2 already in frames | 4 1 6 2 | 4 |
| 7 | 4 | hit | - | 4 already in frames | 4 1 6 2 | 4 |
| 8 | 7 | miss | 4 | frames full; next use 4@#17 > 2@#11 > 1@#10 > 6@#9 -> farthest = 4 | 7 1 6 2 | 5 |
| 9 | 6 | hit | - | 6 already in frames | 7 1 6 2 | 5 |
| 10 | 1 | hit | - | 1 already in frames | 7 1 6 2 | 5 |
| 11 | 2 | hit | - | 2 already in frames | 7 1 6 2 | 5 |
| 12 | 0 | miss | 1 | frames full; next use 1@never > 7@#18 > 2@#15 > 6@#13 -> farthest = 1 | 7 0 6 2 | 6 |
| 13 | 6 | hit | - | 6 already in frames | 7 0 6 2 | 6 |
| 14 | 0 | hit | - | 0 already in frames | 7 0 6 2 | 6 |
| 15 | 2 | hit | - | 2 already in frames | 7 0 6 2 | 6 |
| 16 | 3 | miss | 0 | frames full; next use 0@never > 6@never > 2@#19 > 7@#18 -> farthest = 0 | 7 3 6 2 | 7 |
| 17 | 4 | miss | 3 | frames full; next use 3@never > 6@never > 2@#19 > 7@#18 -> farthest = 3 | 7 4 6 2 | 8 |
| 18 | 7 | hit | - | 7 already in frames | 7 4 6 2 | 8 |
| 19 | 2 | hit | - | 2 already in frames | 7 4 6 2 | 8 |
| 20 | 4 | hit | - | 4 already in frames | 7 4 6 2 | 8 |

**Total page faults = 8** (hits = 20 - 8 = 12, hit ratio = 12 / 20 = 0.6, fault ratio = 8 / 20 = 0.4)

**Answer: page faults = 8**

problem: Paging is used with 8 KB pages. The page table (indexed by page number) is [46, 24, 50, 50, 56]. Translate the logical address 0x1c69 into a physical address.
solution:
**Step-by-step translation**

- convert 0x1c69 to decimal: 1 x 4096 = 4096; 12 x 256 = 3072; 6 x 16 = 96; 9 x 1 = 9
- sum: 4096 + 3072 = 7168, 7168 + 96 = 7264, 7264 + 9 = 7273 -> 0x1c69 = 7273
- page number = floor(7273 / 8192) = 0  (check: 0 x 8192 = 0 <= 7273 < 8192)
- page offset = 7273 - 0 = 7273
- page table[0] = frame 46
- frame base = 46 x 8192 = 376832
- physical address = 376832 + 7273 = 384105

**Physical address = 384105**
- in hexadecimal: 384105 = 0x5dc69

**Answer: physical address = 384105 (0x5dc69)**

problem: I need help with this problem. Currently available: A=4, B=6, C=1, D=3. Allocation = [[2, 3, 0, 5], [0, 3, 2, 1], [0, 1, 1, 1], [7, 3, 0, 3]]. Max = [[8, 4, 3, 5], [0, 8, 6, 1], [0, 2, 1, 8], [8, 6, 2, 7]]. Is the system in a safe state? If so, give a safe sequence.
solution:
**Step 1 - compute Need = Max - Allocation, row by row** (resources A, B, C, D)

- P0: [8, 4, 3, 5] - [2, 3, 0, 5] = [6, 1, 3, 0]
- P1: [0, 8, 6, 1] - [0, 3, 2, 1] = [0, 5, 4, 0]
- P2: [0, 2, 1, 8] - [0, 1, 1, 1] = [0, 1, 0, 7]
- P3: [8, 6, 2, 7] - [7, 3, 0, 3] = [1, 3, 2, 4]

**Step 2 - run the safety algorithm** (scan the processes in order; run the first one whose Need fits in Work, then add its Allocation to Work and scan again)

- Work = Available = [4, 6, 1, 3]
- P0: Need [6, 1, 3, 0] vs Work [4, 6, 1, 3]: 6>4, 1<=6, 3>1, 0<=3 -> cannot run yet
- P1: Need [0, 5, 4, 0] vs Work [4, 6, 1, 3]: 0<=4, 5<=6, 4>1, 0<=3 -> cannot run yet
- P2: Need [0, 1, 0, 7] vs Work [4, 6, 1, 3]: 0<=4, 1<=6, 0<=1, 7>3 -> cannot run yet
- P3: Need [1, 3, 2, 4] vs Work [4, 6, 1, 3]: 1<=4, 3<=6, 2>1, 4>3 -> cannot run yet

**Step 3 - conclusion**

No remaining process (P0, P1, P2, P3) has a Need that fits in Work [4, 6, 1, 3], so they can never all finish: the system is **NOT in a safe state (UNSAFE)**.

_Unsafe does not mean deadlocked yet: it means a deadlock is possible if the processes request their maximum._

**Answer: UNSAFE, no safe sequence exists**

problem:
Q. A system has resource types A, B, C and processes P0, P1, P2, P3, P4. There are 9 instances of A, 10 instances of B, 14 instances of C in total.

| Process | Alloc A | Alloc B | Alloc C | Max A | Max B | Max C |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| P0 | 1 | 4 | 3 | 4 | 4 | 8 |
| P1 | 1 | 2 | 4 | 4 | 3 | 5 |
| P2 | 1 | 1 | 0 | 2 | 8 | 0 |
| P3 | 1 | 2 | 1 | 6 | 6 | 2 |
| P4 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 3 | 1 | 2 |

Is the system in a safe state? If so, give a safe sequence.
solution:
**Step 0 - Available = Total - (sum of each Allocation column)**

- A: allocated 1 + 1 = 2, 2 + 1 = 3, 3 + 1 = 4, 4 + 0 = 4; available 9 - 4 = 5
- B: allocated 4 + 2 = 6, 6 + 1 = 7, 7 + 2 = 9, 9 + 0 = 9; available 10 - 9 = 1
- C: allocated 3 + 4 = 7, 7 + 0 = 7, 7 + 1 = 8, 8 + 0 = 8; available 14 - 8 = 6
- Available = [5, 1, 6]

**Step 1 - compute Need = Max - Allocation, row by row** (resources A, B, C)

- P0: [4, 4, 8] - [1, 4, 3] = [3, 0, 5]
- P1: [4, 3, 5] - [1, 2, 4] = [3, 1, 1]
- P2: [2, 8, 0] - [1, 1, 0] = [1, 7, 0]
- P3: [6, 6, 2] - [1, 2, 1] = [5, 4, 1]
- P4: [3, 1, 2] - [0, 0, 0] = [3, 1, 2]

**Step 2 - run the safety algorithm** (scan the processes in order; run the first one whose Need fits in Work, then add its Allocation to Work and scan again)

- Work = Available = [5, 1, 6]
- P0: Need [3, 0, 5] vs Work [5, 1, 6]: 3<=5, 0<=1, 5<=6 -> all fit, run it. Work = [5, 1, 6] + Allocation [1, 4, 3] = [6, 5, 9]
- P1: Need [3, 1, 1] vs Work [6, 5, 9]: 3<=6, 1<=5, 1<=9 -> all fit, run it. Work = [6, 5, 9] + Allocation [1, 2, 4] = [7, 7, 13]
- P2: Need [1, 7, 0] vs Work [7, 7, 13]: 1<=7, 7<=7, 0<=13 -> all fit, run it. Work = [7, 7, 13] + Allocation [1, 1, 0] = [8, 8, 13]
- P3: Need [5, 4, 1] vs Work [8, 8, 13]: 5<=8, 4<=8, 1<=13 -> all fit, run it. Work = [8, 8, 13] + Allocation [1, 2, 1] = [9, 10, 14]
- P4: Need [3, 1, 2] vs Work [9, 10, 14]: 3<=9, 1<=10, 2<=14 -> all fit, run it. Work = [9, 10, 14] + Allocation [0, 0, 0] = [9, 10, 14]

**Step 3 - conclusion**

All 5 processes can complete, so the system is in a **SAFE state**.
A safe sequence is **< P0, P1, P2, P3, P4 >**.

_Safe sequences are not unique: any ordering in which each process's Need is met by the running Work vector is equally correct._

**Answer: SAFE, safe sequence < P0, P1, P2, P3, P4 >**

problem: Consider the following. The free holes, in address order, are 61K, 596K, 191K and 93K. Processes of 486K, 104K, 155K, 288K and 258K arrive in that order. Apply first-fit. How much free memory remains in each hole, and in total?
solution:
**Policy: FIRST-fit**

_Rule: scan holes in order and take the FIRST that is large enough; the leftover stays as a smaller hole. A request that fits nowhere must wait._

- holes (free KB, numbered in order): hole 1=61, hole 2=596, hole 3=191, hole 4=93
- request 486: hole 1=61 < 486 no; hole 2=596 >= 486 fits -> first fitting hole = hole 2; 596 - 486 = 110
- request 104: hole 1=61 < 104 no; hole 2=110 >= 104 fits -> first fitting hole = hole 2; 110 - 104 = 6
- request 155: hole 1=61 < 155 no; hole 2=6 < 155 no; hole 3=191 >= 155 fits -> first fitting hole = hole 3; 191 - 155 = 36
- request 288: hole 1=61 < 288 no; hole 2=6 < 288 no; hole 3=36 < 288 no; hole 4=93 < 288 no -> no hole fits -> must WAIT
- request 258: hole 1=61 < 258 no; hole 2=6 < 258 no; hole 3=36 < 258 no; hole 4=93 < 258 no -> no hole fits -> must WAIT

**Placement:** 486 KB -> hole 2; 104 KB -> hole 2; 155 KB -> hole 3; 288 KB -> WAIT; 258 KB -> WAIT
**Remaining free space per hole:** [61, 6, 36, 93]
- Sum of free space: 61 + 6 = 67, 67 + 36 = 103, 103 + 93 = 196
**Total external fragmentation = 196 KB**

**Answer: remaining [61, 6, 36, 93], total free 196 KB**

problem:
A process generates the following sequence of page references:

`2 2 8 2 2 4 6 1 1 7 5 2 5 5 2 3 7 0 1`

given **4** available frames, using the **OPT** replacement policy. How many page faults occur? Show the frame contents after each reference.
solution:
**Policy: OPT, 4 frames** (all empty at the start)

_Rule: on a fault with all frames full, evict the page whose NEXT USE is FARTHEST in the future (never used again = farthest)._

| # | Ref | Result | Evicted | Why | Frames (frame order) | Faults |
|---|-----|--------|---------|-----|--------|--------|
| 1 | 2 | miss | - | free frame (1/4 used) | 2 | 1 |
| 2 | 2 | hit | - | 2 already in frames | 2 | 1 |
| 3 | 8 | miss | - | free frame (2/4 used) | 2 8 | 2 |
| 4 | 2 | hit | - | 2 already in frames | 2 8 | 2 |
| 5 | 2 | hit | - | 2 already in frames | 2 8 | 2 |
| 6 | 4 | miss | - | free frame (3/4 used) | 2 8 4 | 3 |
| 7 | 6 | miss | - | free frame (4/4 used) | 2 8 4 6 | 4 |
| 8 | 1 | miss | 8 | frames full; next use 8@never > 4@never > 6@never > 2@#12 -> farthest = 8 | 2 1 4 6 | 5 |
| 9 | 1 | hit | - | 1 already in frames | 2 1 4 6 | 5 |
| 10 | 7 | miss | 4 | frames full; next use 4@never > 6@never > 1@#19 > 2@#12 -> farthest = 4 | 2 1 7 6 | 6 |
| 11 | 5 | miss | 6 | frames full; next use 6@never > 1@#19 > 7@#17 > 2@#12 -> farthest = 6 | 2 1 7 5 | 7 |
| 12 | 2 | hit | - | 2 already in frames | 2 1 7 5 | 7 |
| 13 | 5 | hit | - | 5 already in frames | 2 1 7 5 | 7 |
| 14 | 5 | hit | - | 5 already in frames | 2 1 7 5 | 7 |
| 15 | 2 | hit | - | 2 already in frames | 2 1 7 5 | 7 |
| 16 | 3 | miss | 2 | frames full; next use 2@never > 5@never > 1@#19 > 7@#17 -> farthest = 2 | 3 1 7 5 | 8 |
| 17 | 7 | hit | - | 7 already in frames | 3 1 7 5 | 8 |
| 18 | 0 | miss | 3 | frames full; next use 3@never > 7@never > 5@never > 1@#19 -> farthest = 3 | 0 1 7 5 | 9 |
| 19 | 1 | hit | - | 1 already in frames | 0 1 7 5 | 9 |

**Total page faults = 9** (hits = 19 - 9 = 10, hit ratio = 10 / 19 = 0.5263, fault ratio = 9 / 19 = 0.4737)

**Answer: page faults = 9**

- 0 -> 249: 249 - 0 = 249; running total 218 + 249 = 467

- 241 -> 222: 241 - 222 = 19; running total 475 + 19 = 494

**Service order:** 204 -> 201 -> 98 -> 91 -> 59 -> 0 -> 249 -> 241 -> 222
**Total head movement = 494 cylinders**
- Average seek length = 494 / 7 = 70.57
- _Convention: this total counts the return jump of 249 cylinders. If your course excludes the jump, the total is 494 - 249 = 245._

**Answer: order 204 -> 201 -> 98 -> 91 -> 59 -> 0 -> 249 -> 241 -> 222; total head movement = 494 cylinders**

problem:
Question: Consider 4 processes and 3 resource types (A, B, C). The available vector is <4, 4, 6>.

| Process | Alloc A | Alloc B | Alloc C | Max A | Max B | Max C |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| T1 | 3 | 0 | 6 | 5 | 0 | 7 |
| T2 | 0 | 0 | 4 | 3 | 4 | 7 |
| T3 | 7 | 0 | 1 | 8 | 2 | 2 |
| T4 | 0 | 2 | 0 | 7 | 2 | 0 |

Use the Banker's algorithm to check whether the state is safe.
solution:
**Step 1 - compute Need = Max - Allocation, row by row** (resources A, B, C)

- T1: [5, 0, 7] - [3, 0, 6] = [2, 0, 1]
- T2: [3, 4, 7] - [0, 0, 4] = [3, 4, 3]
- T3: [8, 2, 2] - [7, 0, 1] = [1, 2, 1]
- T4: [7, 2, 0] - [0, 2, 0] = [7, 0, 0]

**Step 2 - run the safety algorithm** (scan the processes in order; run the first one whose Need fits in Work, then add its Allocation to Work and scan again)

- Work = Available = [4, 4, 6]
- T1: Need [2, 0, 1] vs Work [4, 4, 6]: 2<=4, 0<=4, 1<=6 -> all fit, run it. Work = [4, 4, 6] + Allocation [3, 0, 6] = [7, 4, 12]
- T2: Need [3, 4, 3] vs Work [7, 4, 12]: 3<=7, 4<=4, 3<=12 -> all fit, run it. Work = [7, 4, 12] + Allocation [0, 0, 4] = [7, 4, 16]
- T3: Need [1, 2, 1] vs Work [7, 4, 16]: 1<=7, 2<=4, 1<=16 -> all fit, run it. Work = [7, 4, 16] + Allocation [7, 0, 1] = [14, 4, 17]
- T4: Need [7, 0, 0] vs Work [14, 4, 17]: 7<=14, 0<=4, 0<=17 -> all fit, run it. Work = [14, 4, 17] + Allocation [0, 2, 0] = [14, 6, 17]

**Step 3 - conclusion**

All 4 processes can complete, so the system is in a **SAFE state**.
A safe sequence is **< T1, T2, T3, T4 >**.

_Safe sequences are not unique: any ordering in which each process's Need is met by the running Work vector is equally correct._

**Answer: SAFE, safe sequence < T1, T2, T3, T4 >**

- P1: Need [0, 4, 2, 0]
- P2: Need [4, 1, 0, 1]

- request 45: hole 1=92 >= 45 fits; hole 2=459 >= 45 fits; hole 3=166 >= 45 fits; hole 4=209 >= 45 fits; hole 5=218 >= 45 fits; hole 6=510 >= 45 fits -> largest fitting: 510 > 459 > 218 > 209 > 166 > 92 -> hole 6; 510 - 45 = 465
- request 245: hole 1=92 < 245 no; hole 2=459 >= 245 fits; hole 3=166 < 245 no; hole 4=209 < 245 no; hole 5=218 < 245 no; hole 6=465 >= 245 fits -> largest fitting: 465 > 459 -> hole 6; 465 - 245 = 220
- request 412: hole 1=92 < 412 no; hole 2=459 >= 412 fits; hole 3=166 < 412 no; hole 4=209 < 412 no; hole 5=218 < 412 no; hole 6=220 < 412 no -> largest fitting: 459 -> hole 2; 459 - 412 = 47
- request 469: hole 1=92 < 469 no; hole 2=47 < 469 no; hole 3=166 < 469 no; hole 4=209 < 469 no; hole 5=218 < 469 no; hole 6=220 < 469 no -> no hole fits -> must WAIT

**Placement:** 45 KB -> hole 6; 245 KB -> hole 6; 412 KB -> hole 2; 469 KB -> WAIT
**Remaining free space per hole:** [92, 47, 166, 209, 218, 220]
- Sum of free space: 92 + 47 = 139, 139 + 166 = 305, 305 + 209 = 514, 514 + 218 = 732, 732 + 220 = 952
**Total external fragmentation = 952 KB**

**Answer: 45 KB -> hole 6; 245 KB -> hole 6; 412 KB -> hole 2; 469 KB -> WAIT**

problem:
| Process | Arrival Time | Burst Time |
|---|---|---|
| alpha | 0 | 1 |
| beta | 2 | 4 |
| gamma | 3 | 9 |
| delta | 4 | 3 |
| epsilon | 6 | 7 |

Using highest response ratio next scheduling, compute the average waiting and turnaround times.
solution:
**Algorithm: HRRN (highest response ratio next)**

**Step 1 - build the schedule**

_Rule: whenever the CPU is free, compute each ready process's response ratio = (waiting + burst) / burst and run the HIGHEST ratio to completion (ties: earlier arrival, then name)._

- t=0: only alpha is ready -> run alpha, done at 0 + 1 = 1
- t=1: no process has arrived -> CPU idle until t=2
- t=2: only beta is ready -> run beta, done at 2 + 4 = 6
- t=6: ratios: gamma waited 6 - 3 = 3, (3 + 9) / 9 = 1.33, delta waited 6 - 4 = 2, (2 + 3) / 3 = 1.67, epsilon waited 6 - 6 = 0, (0 + 7) / 7 = 1.00; order delta(1.67) > gamma(1.33) > epsilon(1.00) -> run delta, done at 6 + 3 = 9
- t=9: ratios: gamma waited 9 - 3 = 6, (6 + 9) / 9 = 1.67, epsilon waited 9 - 6 = 3, (3 + 7) / 7 = 1.43; order gamma(1.67) > epsilon(1.43) -> run gamma, done at 9 + 9 = 18
- t=18: only epsilon is ready -> run epsilon, done at 18 + 7 = 25

**Step 2 - Gantt chart:** alpha[0-1] beta[2-6] delta[6-9] gamma[9-18] epsilon[18-25]

**Step 3 - per-process times** (Turnaround = Completion - Arrival; Waiting = Turnaround - Burst)

| Process | Arrival | Burst | Completion | Turnaround  | Waiting     |
|---------|---------|-------|------------|-------------|-------------|
| alpha   | 0       | 1     | 1          | 1 - 0 = 1   | 1 - 1 = 0   |
| beta    | 2       | 4     | 6          | 6 - 2 = 4   | 4 - 4 = 0   |
| delta   | 4       | 3     | 9          | 9 - 4 = 5   | 5 - 3 = 2   |
| epsilon | 6       | 7     | 25         | 25 - 6 = 19 | 19 - 7 = 12 |
| gamma   | 3       | 9     | 18         | 18 - 3 = 15 | 15 - 9 = 6  |

**Step 4 - averages**

- Sum of waiting times: 0 + 0 = 0, 0 + 2 = 2, 2 + 12 = 14, 14 + 6 = 20
- Average waiting time = 20 / 5 = **4.0**
- Sum of turnaround times: 1 + 4 = 5, 5 + 5 = 10, 10 + 19 = 29, 29 + 15 = 44
- Average turnaround time = 44 / 5 = **8.8**

**Answer: average waiting time = 4.0, average turnaround time = 8.8**

problem:
A system has resource types A, B, C, D and processes P1, P2, P3 and P4. The available vector is (4,3,4,2).

| Process | Alloc A | Alloc B | Alloc C | Alloc D | Need A | Need B | Need C | Need D |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| P1 | 7 | 1 | 4 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 6 |
| P2 | 1 | 0 | 0 | 1 | 6 | 0 | 0 | 4 |
| P3 | 0 | 5 | 0 | 4 | 2 | 0 | 3 | 0 |
| P4 | 0 | 0 | 3 | 4 | 7 | 0 | 1 | 2 |

Request_P3 = [2, 0, 3, 0]. Apply the resource-request algorithm.
solution:
**Step 1 - Need is given directly** (Need = Max - Allocation)

- P1: Need [0, 0, 0, 6]
- P2: Need [6, 0, 0, 4]
- P3: Need [2, 0, 3, 0]
- P4: Need [7, 0, 1, 2]

**Step 2 - apply the three tests of the resource-request algorithm**

- Test 1: Request [2, 0, 3, 0] vs Need [2, 0, 3, 0]: 2<=2, 0<=0, 3<=3, 0<=0 -> OK
- Test 2: Request [2, 0, 3, 0] vs Available [4, 3, 4, 2]: 2<=4, 0<=3, 3<=4, 0<=2 -> OK
- Test 3: pretend to grant. Available = [4, 3, 4, 2] - [2, 0, 3, 0] = [2, 3, 1, 2]; Allocation[P3] = [2, 5, 3, 4]. Now run the safety algorithm.
- Work = Available = [2, 3, 1, 2]
- P1: Need [0, 0, 0, 6] vs Work [2, 3, 1, 2]: 0<=2, 0<=3, 0<=1, 6>2 -> cannot run yet
- P2: Need [6, 0, 0, 4] vs Work [2, 3, 1, 2]: 6>2, 0<=3, 0<=1, 4>2 -> cannot run yet
- P3: Need [0, 0, 0, 0] vs Work [2, 3, 1, 2]: 0<=2, 0<=3, 0<=1, 0<=2 -> all fit, run it. Work = [2, 3, 1, 2] + Allocation [2, 5, 3, 4] = [4, 8, 4, 6]
- P1: Need [0, 0, 0, 6] vs Work [4, 8, 4, 6]: 0<=4, 0<=8, 0<=4, 6<=6 -> all fit, run it. Work = [4, 8, 4, 6] + Allocation [7, 1, 4, 0] = [11, 9, 8, 6]
- P2: Need [6, 0, 0, 4] vs Work [11, 9, 8, 6]: 6<=11, 0<=9, 0<=8, 4<=6 -> all fit, run it. Work = [11, 9, 8, 6] + Allocation [1, 0, 0, 1] = [12, 9, 8, 7]
- P4: Need [7, 0, 1, 2] vs Work [12, 9, 8, 7]: 7<=12, 0<=9, 1<=8, 2<=7 -> all fit, run it. Work = [12, 9, 8, 7] + Allocation [0, 0, 3, 4] = [12, 9, 11, 11]
- SAFE. Safe sequence: < P3, P1, P2, P4 >
- Resulting state is SAFE (sequence < P3, P1, P2, P4 >) -> GRANT the request

**Conclusion: the request is GRANTED.**

**Answer: GRANTED**

problem: Can you solve this step by step? The disk has 300 cylinders (0 to 299). The disk head starts at track 111. Pending requests (cylinders): {199, 260, 216, 115, 226, 150}. The previous request served was at cylinder 101. Using C-LOOK scheduling, give the order in which requests are served and the total head movement.
solution:
**Policy: CLOOK**

- direction: previous request 101 < head 111, so the head is moving UP
- sorted requests: [115, 150, 199, 216, 226, 260]; below head 111: []; at/above head: [115, 150, 199, 216, 226, 260]
- C-LOOK, head moving UP, towards higher cylinders: service [115, 150, 199, 216, 226, 260], jump to the farthest pending request, continue up through []
- 111 -> 115: 115 - 111 = 4; running total 0 + 4 = 4
- 115 -> 150: 150 - 115 = 35; running total 4 + 35 = 39
- 150 -> 199: 199 - 150 = 49; running total 39 + 49 = 88
- 199 -> 216: 216 - 199 = 17; running total 88 + 17 = 105
- 216 -> 226: 226 - 216 = 10; running total 105 + 10 = 115
- 226 -> 260: 260 - 226 = 34; running total 115 + 34 = 149

**Service order:** 115 -> 150 -> 199 -> 216 -> 226 -> 260
**Total head movement = 149 cylinders**
- Average seek length = 149 / 6 = 24.83

**Answer: order 115 -> 150 -> 199 -> 216 -> 226 -> 260; total head movement = 149 cylinders**

problem:
A process generates the following sequence of page references:

`5, 1, 5, 0, 5, 2, 4, 0, 7, 8, 7, 0, 2, 1, 9`

and the process is allocated **4 page frames**, using the **LRU** replacement policy. How many page faults result? Include a step-by-step trace.
solution:
**Policy: LRU, 4 frames** (all empty at the start)

_Rule: on a fault with all frames full, evict the page used LEAST RECENTLY._

| # | Ref | Result | Evicted | Why | Frames (least recently used first) | Faults |
|---|-----|--------|---------|-----|--------|--------|
| 1 | 5 | miss | - | free frame (1/4 used) | 5 | 1 |
| 2 | 1 | miss | - | free frame (2/4 used) | 5 1 | 2 |
| 3 | 5 | hit | - | 5 already in frames | 1 5 | 2 |
| 4 | 0 | miss | - | free frame (3/4 used) | 1 5 0 | 3 |
| 5 | 5 | hit | - | 5 already in frames | 1 0 5 | 3 |
| 6 | 2 | miss | - | free frame (4/4 used) | 1 0 5 2 | 4 |
| 7 | 4 | miss | 1 | frames full; last used 1@#2 < 0@#4 < 5@#5 < 2@#6 -> least recent = 1 | 0 5 2 4 | 5 |
| 8 | 0 | hit | - | 0 already in frames | 5 2 4 0 | 5 |
| 9 | 7 | miss | 5 | frames full; last used 5@#5 < 2@#6 < 4@#7 < 0@#8 -> least recent = 5 | 2 4 0 7 | 6 |
| 10 | 8 | miss | 2 | frames full; last used 2@#6 < 4@#7 < 0@#8 < 7@#9 -> least recent = 2 | 4 0 7 8 | 7 |
| 11 | 7 | hit | - | 7 already in frames | 4 0 8 7 | 7 |
| 12 | 0 | hit | - | 0 already in frames | 4 8 7 0 | 7 |
| 13 | 2 | miss | 4 | frames full; last used 4@#7 < 8@#10 < 7@#11 < 0@#12 -> least recent = 4 | 8 7 0 2 | 8 |
| 14 | 1 | miss | 8 | frames full; last used 8@#10 < 7@#11 < 0@#12 < 2@#13 -> least recent = 8 | 7 0 2 1 | 9 |
| 15 | 9 | miss | 7 | frames full; last used 7@#11 < 0@#12 < 2@#13 < 1@#14 -> least recent = 7 | 0 2 1 9 | 10 |

**Total page faults = 10** (hits = 15 - 10 = 5, hit ratio = 5 / 15 = 0.3333, fault ratio = 10 / 15 = 0.6667)

**Answer: page faults = 10**

problem: Here is an exam question. Available = [4, 1, 3]. Allocation = [[1, 3, 1], [2, 0, 3], [1, 2, 3], [4, 1, 2]]. Max = [[4, 6, 2], [6, 3, 3], [5, 2, 5], [6, 1, 4]]. Find a safe sequence, if one exists.
solution:
**Step 1 - compute Need = Max - Allocation, row by row** (resources A, B, C)

- P0: [4, 6, 2] - [1, 3, 1] = [3, 3, 1]
- P1: [6, 3, 3] - [2, 0, 3] = [4, 3, 0]
- P2: [5, 2, 5] - [1, 2, 3] = [4, 0, 2]
- P3: [6, 1, 4] - [4, 1, 2] = [2, 0, 2]

**Step 2 - run the safety algorithm** (scan the processes in order; run the first one whose Need fits in Work, then add its Allocation to Work and scan again)

- Work = Available = [4, 1, 3]
- P0: Need [3, 3, 1] vs Work [4, 1, 3]: 3<=4, 3>1, 1<=3 -> cannot run yet
- P1: Need [4, 3, 0] vs Work [4, 1, 3]: 4<=4, 3>1, 0<=3 -> cannot run yet
- P2: Need [4, 0, 2] vs Work [4, 1, 3]: 4<=4, 0<=1, 2<=3 -> all fit, run it. Work = [4, 1, 3] + Allocation [1, 2, 3] = [5, 3, 6]
- P0: Need [3, 3, 1] vs Work [5, 3, 6]: 3<=5, 3<=3, 1<=6 -> all fit, run it. Work = [5, 3, 6] + Allocation [1, 3, 1] = [6, 6, 7]
- P1: Need [4, 3, 0] vs Work [6, 6, 7]: 4<=6, 3<=6, 0<=7 -> all fit, run it. Work = [6, 6, 7] + Allocation [2, 0, 3] = [8, 6, 10]
- P3: Need [2, 0, 2] vs Work [8, 6, 10]: 2<=8, 0<=6, 2<=10 -> all fit, run it. Work = [8, 6, 10] + Allocation [4, 1, 2] = [12, 7, 12]

**Step 3 - conclusion**

All 4 processes can complete, so the system is in a **SAFE state**.
A safe sequence is **< P2, P0, P1, P3 >**.

_Safe sequences are not unique: any ordering in which each process's Need is met by the running Work vector is equally correct._

**Answer: SAFE, safe sequence < P2, P0, P1, P3 >**

problem:
An I/O subsystem with cylinders 0-199 has its head at **132**. Queued requests:

`137, 41, 175, 45, 66, 14, 125, 118`

Using **CLOOK** scheduling. The head is currently moving toward lower cylinder numbers. Determine the seek sequence and total head movement.
solution:
**Policy: CLOOK**

- sorted requests: [14, 41, 45, 66, 118, 125, 137, 175]; below head 132: [14, 41, 45, 66, 118, 125]; at/above head: [137, 175]
- C-LOOK, head moving DOWN, towards cylinder 0: service [125, 118, 66, 45, 41, 14], jump to the farthest pending request, continue down through [175, 137]
- 132 -> 125: 132 - 125 = 7; running total 0 + 7 = 7
- 125 -> 118: 125 - 118 = 7; running total 7 + 7 = 14
- 118 -> 66: 118 - 66 = 52; running total 14 + 52 = 66
- 66 -> 45: 66 - 45 = 21; running total 66 + 21 = 87
- 45 -> 41: 45 - 41 = 4; running total 87 + 4 = 91
- 41 -> 14: 41 - 14 = 27; running total 91 + 27 = 118
- 14 -> 175: 175 - 14 = 161; running total 118 + 161 = 279
- 175 -> 137: 175 - 137 = 38; running total 279 + 38 = 317

**Service order:** 125 -> 118 -> 66 -> 45 -> 41 -> 14 -> 175 -> 137
**Total head movement = 317 cylinders**
- Average seek length = 317 / 8 = 39.62
- _Convention: this total counts the return jump of 161 cylinders. If your course excludes the jump, the total is 317 - 161 = 156._

**Answer: total head movement = 317 cylinders**
